Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 10 betting picks: Ice-cold human seeks a rebound as AI gains ground
articles.excerpt:
Tom Brady lists his top 10 teams for Week 9 which include the Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs and more!

I am officially ice cold. I followed up the disaster that was Week 8 (wh...
articles.body_text:
Tom Brady lists his top 10 teams for Week 9 which include the Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs and more!

I am officially ice cold. I followed up the disaster that was Week 8 (which I’m still not talking about) with a losing slate in Week 9. This serves as an important reminder to everyone out there: being a winning bettor in the NFL is very, very difficult.

It’s hard to find value because the NFL is one of the most heavily bet leagues in the country. There’s an enormous amount of information available, and both sportsbooks and sharp bettors spend all week picking these games apart.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

NFL WEEK 9 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS, 49ERS, PACKERS LOOK SUPER; RAMS FINALLY OVER .500

The books are very good at pricing NFL bets, so the edges are difficult to find. I think there’s more room to find value in less-bet markets, like college basketball games featuring unranked and lesser-known schools.

Does that mean we’re going to quit? Of course not. A profitable season in NFL betting, especially when I’ve committed to five bets per week, is something worth bragging about. So the goal is to get back to profitability.

It feels like I've been losing more than Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni over the past two weeks. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Both of us get five selections from the same odds board, with no bet priced worse than -120. Odds were taken from the board supplied Thursday at noon ET.

Stakes are adjusted so every winning bet produces one unit of profit. For example, -110 requires risking 1.10 units, while +110 requires approximately 0.91 units. A push returns the stake and counts as zero units.

The Denver Broncos once again benefited from some questionable officiating, and it helped sink our Panthers bet. I’m not bitter, though. The Raiders and Vikings were clean whiffs, and the latter served as a very important reminder: never wager your hard-earned money on Carson Wentz.

If you remove GPT’s worst two weeks (Week 1 and Week 8), the robot is having an OK year: 18-16-1 and up 0.77 units. Unfortunately for the AI, we don’t just forget about the disasters. Unfortunately for me, too, because I’d love to dump that Week 8 stinker (which I’m still not talking about).

Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week: 5-3, +1.83 units

At least the Bucs got the Plug Your Nose bet back in the win column. Small victories.

Washington Commanders at New York Giants, Thursday Night Football

Betting a road team on Thursday Night Football is always scary, but I’m a Jayden Daniels truther. What can I say? J.J. McCarthy has given the New York Giants some life, and John Harbaugh remains one of the NFL’s best coaches. But New York has also been incredibly fortunate to reach 5-2-1, with four of those wins coming against the Cowboys, Titans, Cardinals and Eagles.

I'm a Jayden Daniels truther. (Getty Images)

Washington hung tough against the Rams last week and held a second-half lead. I think Daniels wills the Commanders to a win Thursday night, but I’ll still take the two points just in case they tie again. That’s a joke. Kind of.

Jayden Daniels hurt the Giants with his legs in the first meeting, and that’s Washington’s best answer to New York’s blitz. I worry about how much the Commanders can get on the ground from anyone else with Jacory Croskey-Merritt out. I passed because even a three-point Giants win is enough to beat this ticket.

New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET, in Munich

New England headed to Munich a day ahead of Detroit, and I think that works in the Patriots’ favor. Plus, they’re coming off a terrible performance against the Green Bay Packers, and I think they’ll be extremely motivated to prove that was a fluke.

The Lions have won four straight, but I’m still not sold on Detroit. For an offense that’s supposed to be among the most explosive in the league, the Lions are actually winning with defense and haven’t scored more than 20 points in their past three games. I don’t think that’s going to work against Mike Vrabel’s squad, so I’ll take the points with the Pats.

I lean New England here. Drake Maye can attack a Detroit secondary that’s given up plenty of big plays, and getting the full field goal matters in a game I expect to be close. Detroit’s pass rush against New England’s protection is what kept me off it at -115.

Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

The Browns just aren’t that good. I said it. Having a quarterback controversy between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders perfectly encapsulates where this team finds itself through nine weeks. Watson has been named the starter against Houston, but that doesn’t make me feel any better about Cleveland.

SHEDEUR SANDERS MAKES CASE TO REPLACE DESHAUN WATSON IN BROWNS' OVERTIME LOSS TO SAINTS

The Texans haven't been super impressive, either, but this team is much better than Cleveland. Even on the road, I think the Texans win by at least a touchdown.

Houston’s pass rush is the best reason to lay the points. The Texans have 29 sacks, and Cleveland has struggled to protect its quarterbacks. Deshaun Watson’s return gives the Browns a better chance to hang around, and their defense can keep the game close. I lean Houston, but I’d want -4½.

Miami Dolphins at Indianapolis Colts, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

I know what you’re thinking: "Are you nuts?!" This is a game featuring Kyle McCord and Daniel Jones as the starting quarterbacks, and the Colts have traded Quenton Nelson, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

But I have a sneaking suspicion that Jonathan Taylor is due for a vintage JT game and will help the Colts put some points on the board. Plus, McCord and Jones are each liable to make a mistake or two that leads to easy scoring opportunities for the other team.

Jonathan Taylor is due for a huge game with multiple explosive plays, which is why I like the over in this one. (Getty Images)

For the first time, Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week is a total. Because, again, we’re counting on teams quarterbacked by Kyle McCord and Daniel Jones to combine for at least 39 points.

This nearly made my card. Jonathan Taylor has a good matchup against a Miami front that lost Zach Sieler, and 20-19 gets you over. My hesitation is how much Miami can contribute in Kyle McCord’s first NFL start. Indianapolis also just traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, so both passing games come with questions.

Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday Night Football

Everyone is talking about the Bengals as Super Bowl contenders, myself included, and this pick doesn’t change my mind. I’m simply fading public perception. If Cincinnati is a true Super Bowl contender, why is it only a 3½-point favorite at home in a massive primetime showdown with the Paycor Stadium crowd ready to rock? It seems like the books know something we don’t.

I’m not a huge believer in Pittsburgh, but the Steelers typically play the Bengals well. Using Bet Legend Pro’s historical lines, Cincinnati is 5-10 against the spread against Pittsburgh under Zac Taylor, including 2-5 as a favorite and 1-2 as a home favorite. The Bengals are also 1-6 ATS in the matchup since 2023.

That’s enough for me to think Pittsburgh keeps this AFC North showdown within a field goal.

We’re on the same side here. Pittsburgh won the first meeting and comes off a bye while Cincinnati returns from Madrid. The Steelers can lean on the run and keep Joe Burrow off the field. Burrow’s success against zone gives Cincinnati a good chance to win, which is exactly why I want the hook. A Bengals field-goal win cashes for both of us.

For full transparency, I used GPT-6.1 Sol with the thinking effort set to ultra. I supplied the odds board captured Thursday at noon ET and gave it the following prompt:

"Pick your five best bets for Week 10 based on the odds provided. No bet can be priced worse than -120. Review every spread, total and moneyline that falls within those parameters and determine whether it belongs among your five picks. Explain exactly why you’re selecting each of the five bets. Also explain exactly why you’re passing on the eligible bets you don’t select. Use at least 10 different sources for each game so you have a broad understanding of everything surrounding each game. Before delivering the results, do a fact-check and ensure that everything is correct."

Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Atlanta’s offense runs through Bijan Robinson, and Kansas City has the run defense to keep him from dictating the game. That puts more on Michael Penix Jr. against a defense allowing 17.9 points per game. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after hurting his elbow, and Atlanta just traded safety Jessie Bates III.

GPT likes Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker to help the Chiefs score enough points to cover on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. (Getty Images)

The Falcons can get pressure, so Mahomes’ elbow is worth watching. At even money, I’m willing to lay the extra half-point because Kansas City has the better matchup on both sides of the ball.

GPT’s projected score: Chiefs 26, Falcons 20

Kansas City has a massive advantage at both head coach and quarterback, but I'm wary of laying three points and the hook with the Chiefs as a road favorite in a game where the public also figures to want to hammer the Chiefs.

Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Minnesota has scored 16, 15 and six points in its last three games. Its defense still leads the NFL at 14.5 points allowed per game. If Kirk Cousins starts, he’ll have only a few days to get reacquainted with the offense after Tuesday’s trade. Green Bay also expects to be without Josh Jacobs after he fractured a finger.

Jordan Love just threw for 372 yards, and the first meeting produced 61 points. I’m still taking the under because Minnesota can make things harder on Love and has struggled to finish drives of its own.

GPT’s projected score: Packers 21, Vikings 17

NFL TRADE DEADLINE WINNERS AND LOSERS, INCLUDING DIANNA RUSSINI AND KIRK COUSINS

I like this pick. With the Packers coming off a 45-point explosion against the Patriots, this is the perfect time to fade what we saw most recently. The Vikings defense is legit and Minnesota figures to be relatively conservative on offense with Kirk Cousins making his 2026 debut for the team.

Buffalo Bills at New York Jets, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Buffalo leads the NFL at 32 points per game, and James Cook gets a Jets defense that has allowed more than 140 rushing yards per game over its last four. The Jets settled for four field goals against Kansas City last week. That’s a problem if Josh Allen and Cook build an early lead.

Josh Allen is a stud, but 8 points is a lot to lay on the road against a divisional matchup. (Matt Krohn-Imagn Images)

Buffalo is on a short week and has injuries up front, so there’s some risk in laying eight on the road. I’ll take the matchup, with a push if the Bills win by exactly eight.

Betting against the Bills bit me last week, so this was an easy pass for me. Obviously, Buffalo deserves to be a heavy favorite, but I couldn't bring myself to lay this many points on the road in a divisional game.

San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

Both offenses rank in the top six in scoring, so I understand why the total is this high. I’m counting on San Francisco’s defense to keep Dallas from doing its share. The 49ers allow 19.5 points per game, and the Cowboys lost tight end Jake Ferguson to a knee injury.

San Francisco could score in the 30s against this Dallas defense. That’s the biggest risk, but 56½ gives us room for both teams to score. The 49ers can put up 31 and Dallas can score 24 and the under still cashes.

GPT’s projected score: 49ers 30, Cowboys 24

I like this pick from a pure numbers standpoint because 56½ points is a ton for an NFL game. In fact, if the number closes here, it would be the highest total in the league this season. Both teams can score, obviously, but when a game can finish 30-24 and still hit the under, I'd rather be on that side.

Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday Night Football

Pittsburgh won the first meeting 30-27 and comes off a bye while Cincinnati returns from Madrid. The Steelers allow 18 points per game and have a favorable rushing matchup that can help keep Joe Burrow on the sideline.

Burrow is the reason I want the hook. He completes a league-best 74.7% of his passes against zone, and Pittsburgh plays zone on more than 84% of opposing dropbacks. Cincinnati can win that matchup and take the game by a field goal. Pittsburgh +3½ still cashes.

GPT’s projected score: Bengals 24, Steelers 21

Well, if you want my analysis on this pick, just read what I wrote when I made the same pick. Theoretically, I should be more confident now, but suddenly I'm worried. That can't be good, right?

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

OK, that's it for Week 10! I feel extremely confident in this card and I think this is the one that turns it all around. And, if not, you know the drill: I'm just not going to talk about it.

articles.title: Teachers union spent nearly $8M to crush school choice, biological sports measures, report finds
articles.excerpt:
Defending Education’s Erika Sanzi discusses internal NEA documents and criticizes the union’s political spending and opposition to school choice.

The country's largest teachers union and its affiliat...
articles.body_text:
Defending Education’s Erika Sanzi discusses internal NEA documents and criticizes the union’s political spending and opposition to school choice.

The country's largest teachers union and its affiliates poured nearly $7.8 million into ballot fights across three states in 2026, as internal documents outlined strategies to target voucher programs and other conservative initiatives, according to Defending Education (DE).

In a recent report, the education watchdog uncovered a guidance document from the National Education Association (NEA) which stated that "unions may spend unlimited amounts from their general treasuries on ballot measures in any state, subject to any state affiliate agreements to address specific state laws." Additionally, DE found that the NEA calls for providing "strategic and financial assistance" to defeat unfriendly ballot measures.

DE senior director of communications Erika Sanzi, a former teacher and NEA member, told Fox News Digital that the union has shifted towards politics over the years. She said that instead of talking about education, the union has become focused on issues like the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, climate change and gender ideology, among others.

"I 100% believe that the union has done a lot of damage and continues to do a lot damage," Sanzi told Fox News Digital. "I also think that they've become much more political and much more ideological than they used to be."

UNEARTHED FILING SHOWS LARGEST TEACHERS UNIONS POURED OVER $900 MILLION INTO POLITICAL ACTIVITIES

Internal NEA documents outline plans to provide strategic and financial assistance to oppose ballot measures, according to a Defending Education report. (Celal Güne/Anadolu via Getty Images)

The financial findings in DE's report show the union's spending on political fights across the country.

On Sept. 30, 2026, the Arizona Education Association sent $75,000 to Will of The People PAC, a group that opposed Proposition 318, according to DE. The proposition was approved and will require all schools and athletic associations to restrict access to private spaces and sports participation based on biological sex.

The Washington state NEA affiliate Washington Education Association contributed more than $391,000 to No Hate in WA State, DE found. The group opposed two ballot measures, one of which was aimed at restoring parents' rights in public schools. The other ballot measure, which was approved, will require sex verification for participation in women's sports.

In Alaska, the NEA Advocacy Fund contributed $250,000 to the group "No on 2," which opposed Alaska's Ballot Measure No. 2, which sought to repeal the state's top-four ranked-choice voting system.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

Defending Education's report details the National Education Association's push to fund political fights. (Nate Smallwood/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The grassroots group found that in the first two quarters of 2026, the Protect Education, Accountability Now PAC received $7,075,438.33 from the Arizona Education Association and the NEA for an anti-school choice campaign. DE said in its report that "the PAC appears to be run and operated by the president of an NEA local affiliate – Kyrene Education Association."

Fox News Digital was unable to independently confirm whether the PAC and the Kyrene Education Association share leadership.

Beyond the contributions detailed in the report, the NEA has made its opposition to voucher programs, arguing that they take away resources from public schools and have racist origins. A Feb. 13, 2026, post on NEA Today, the union's blog, claimed that "voucher expansion is re-segregating schools by race and income and reflects a policy rooted in resistance to school integration."

However, Sanzi told Fox News Digital that there is a fundamental misunderstanding of what school choice actually means.

"What I try to remind people of is school choice doesn't mean that the public school won't be the choice," Sanzi told Fox News Digital. "For the majority of families, the local public school is the choice, it just means that they have other options and alternatives as well."

DENVER MOTHER FIGHTS FOR HER DAUGHTER'S EDUCATION AS ADVOCATES MAKE NATIONWIDE SCHOOL CHOICE PUSH

Internal NEA documents obtained by Defending Education offer a look at the teachers union’s efforts to support political campaigns and preserve membership dues revenue. (Paul Morigi/Getty Images for National Education Association)

DE’s report also examines the NEA’s efforts to preserve dues revenue as states restrict payroll deductions.

In 2025, the NEA released a document titled "AutoPay Playbook," which was obtained by DE. The playbook lays out the union's objections to payroll deduction bans, which the union argued were intended "to force affiliates into all-consuming conversion campaigns that prevent our union from building the power we need to protect public education."

The NEA’s playbook describes proactively moving members to AutoPay as "the only way to neutralize this threat and protect our power" in the face of payroll deduction bans. The union warns that fast-moving state legislation can leave affiliates with "near-impossible timelines" to make the switch.

The AutoPay program, according to DE, relies on recurring electronic funds transfers to collect membership dues.

"The idea that they wanna compel people into this AutoPay system, it's in part because it gives all the power to the union versus the school district and the member," Sanzi told Fox News Digital. She added that members could "get stuck" in a subscription model, where payments are continuous and often forgotten about.

Sanzi noted that parents often conflate supporting their children’s teachers with supporting union leadership.

"I think people feel obligated to be in favor of the teacher's union because they hear the word teachers, and they want to be supportive of their children's teachers. But the union and the rank and file teachers are two very different entities," she told Fox News Digital.

The NEA did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Rachel Wolf is a media and culture reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Dianna Russini's cringe podcast debut raises questions about the viability of her comeback
articles.excerpt: Craig Carton holds nothing back as he reacts to former NFL insider Dianna Russini making her controversial sports media return with BetUS following her resignation from The Athletic over her scandal w...
articles.body_text:
Craig Carton holds nothing back as he reacts to former NFL insider Dianna Russini making her controversial sports media return with BetUS following her resignation from The Athletic over her scandal with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.

Dianna Russini debuted her new project with offshore gambling company BetUS on Wednesday. Again, Russini avoided addressing the Mike Vrabel scandal or taking any accountability.

She did, however, joke about memes related to the scandal.

"I’ve seen all the memes and comments … and some of you guys are really funny," Russini said on the "Russin Report."

She referenced a viral AI video showing her playing the saxophone alongside Vrabel. Russini said that if she played an instrument, it would be the saxophone. Later, she credited AI with making her look like an "L.A. 10."

If there was one bright spot in the debut, it was that Russini didn't plead for sympathy, as she did earlier in the week in an interview with People.

DIANNA RUSSINI IS PLANNING A RETURN TO UNKNOWN SPORTS MEDIA POSITION 'NEXT WEEK' AFTER SCANDAL

During that discussion, she claimed she was the victim of "heartbreaking lies" and said she wanted to be an inspiration to other women.

Russini did not specify which claims about her were "lies."

Considering there is photographic evidence of her and Vrabel together dating back seven years, it is hard to dispute that she failed to disclose a personal relationship, romantic or otherwise, with someone she covered and used as a source. That undisclosed relationship was the reason The Athletic gave for finding her in violation of company standards.

Judging by the reaction from various members of the media, Russini did little this week to improve perceptions of her. She continues to handle this poorly, as if she truly believes she did nothing wrong.

That is why the outlook for her new project could be dim.

BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL

ESPN's Dianna Russini was photographed for 201 Magazine at Northern Valley Regional High School in Old Tappan, N.J., on Aug. 24, 2020. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

Unsurprisingly, her first episode drew substantial interest. The website hosting the show, BetUS TV, crashed because of the traffic. The reason for that interest was obvious: People wanted to see whether she would address the scandal. Because she didn't, that interest is unlikely to carry over to future episodes.

Can Russini generate enough interest by discussing football? Given concerns about her credibility and criticism of her lack of accountability, that could be difficult.

Entertaining an audience requires different skills than breaking NFL news. Most successful hosts build a connection with their audience through trust and authenticity.

That will be a hard sell for Dianna Russini.

Split showing Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and NFL reporter Dianna Russini. (Getty Images)

She has become increasingly unlikable and cringeworthy since the scandal began. She talks down to her audience as if she expects everyone to accept that she was simply a victim.

She wasn't. And no honest person could think she was.

Let us know: Do you have any interest in watching Russini host a weekly podcast?

articles.title: Dozens of protesters arrested after staging sit-in at Chuck Schumer’s DC office
articles.excerpt:
Protesters with the Sunrise Movement youth climate group push for new Senate leadership and ending the filibuster

Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were ar...
articles.body_text:
Protesters with the Sunrise Movement youth climate group push for new Senate leadership and ending the filibuster

Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were arrested after staging a sit-in inside Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer’s Washington DC office Thursday

According to the Sunrise Movement, 54 people were arrested, among a few hundred who joined the protest from across the country, including some from New York, which Schumer represents. On its Instagram, the group is fundraising $24,000 to cover the bail fees and any potential legal fees for those arrested.

Capitol police were not immediately available for comment.

In a clip on the Sunrise Movement’s Instagram, with over 40,000 likes at the time of publication, young people sitting on the office floor chanted: “Hey hey, ho ho, Schumer has got to go!” Protesters, including children, held signs reading “The filibuster kills,” “Stop the climate crisis,” and “Schumer: Step up or step aside.”

As Senate Democrats prepare to vote on a majority leader for the upcoming Congress, they’re wrestling with how to navigate what feels like a clear mandate for anti-establishment voices from communities historically underrepresented in federal office to step into leadership. Several Democratic senators have said they will not support Schumer for the position, including Bernie Sanders, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, as well as several members of the freshman class, like Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews.

Some have backed Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen as a challenger, including Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s senator-elect, and 50501, one of the major groups behind the No Kings protests.

The protesters on Thursday delivered a letter to Schumer arguing, per the group’s press release, that “after a collective decade of Schumer leadership it was time for change” and demanding Democrats prioritize ending the filibuster when Congress returns in January.

They also dropped the letters at the offices of every Senate Democrat. According to the Sunrise Movement’s campaigns director, Kidus Girma, Thursday’s action is one of several planned over the next two weeks targeting Senate Democrats and “demanding they actually take action”.

The group has regularly protested against politicians since first making headlines in 2018 with another sit-in targeting then-House speaker Nancy Pelosi, and helped launch calls for a Green New Deal alongside congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who was part of that 2018 sit-in. In the eight years since, Sunrise has supported progressive candidates, and last week, a Sunrise co-founder, Will Lawrence, 36, won his race for a Michigan US House seat after campaigning against datacenters.

“Young people went to Senator Chuck Schumer’s office to demand a Senate majority leader that would fight for the young people who elected a historic blue wave last week. They’re demanding change, not the same old, same old,” said Girma over the phone.

According to early data from Tufts University’s Center for Information and Research on Civic Learning and Engagement (Circle), which monitors youth civic engagement, the 3 November elections saw the second-highest youth turnout for a midterm election in 30 years – following only the 2018 midterms in Donald Trump’s first term.

“Chuck Schumer has been in office longer than I have been alive, and I’m 31 years old,” Girmus said. “[Young people] didn’t vote for a return to the Biden years, but rather a change.”

This isn’t the first sit-in of Schumer’s office organized by young people to happen this week. On Tuesday, three protesters were arrested during a protest by the youth advocacy group Get Free, who were there saying voters “need Democratic leaders to meet the moment lest we repeat history again”, according to executive director Nicole Carty.

Last week, Girma said the election outcome “shows that young people deeply, deeply care about their futures and the current government – but also, they’re making clear demands around how to fix it”.

articles.title: Italy fight back to beat France 3-1 and move top of Nations League group
articles.excerpt:
Francesco Pio Esposito struck twice to inflict a first defeat on Zinedine Zidane as France’s head coach, while Italy stormed back to win 3-1 at San Siro and top their Nations League group.

Michael Ol...
articles.body_text:
Francesco Pio Esposito struck twice to inflict a first defeat on Zinedine Zidane as France’s head coach, while Italy stormed back to win 3-1 at San Siro and top their Nations League group.

Michael Olise profited from a Gianluigi Donnarumma error to put the visitors in front after 10 minutes on Thursday, but Italy hit back through Esposito and Davide Frattesi either side of half-time.

Inter Milan striker Esposito’s second came from the penalty spot after his brother Sebastiano had earlier fired a spot kick wide, while France were twice denied by the woodwork in an entertaining encounter.

The result sent Italy top of Group A1 on 10 points, level with France but above them on head-to-head record, while Belgium are third on nine points after inflicting a fifth straight defeat on rock-bottom Turkiye.

France were without star attackers Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele through injury, but it did not show as they made an electric start in pouring rain in Milan.

Desire Doue hit the side netting and first-time captain Adrien Rabiot tested Donnarumma before Lucas Da Cunha’s rasping half-volley flew narrowly wide.

But the opener was gifted to France when Donnarumma passed the ball straight to Olise, who skipped past a defender before firing home his fifth goal in five Nations League games – a record only bettered by England captain Harry Kane’s seven.

The hosts struck back in the 26th minute with their first chance of the game when Nicolo Cambiaghi drove to the byline and cut back a cross, which Esposito converted with a deft touch.

The goal brought San Siro to life as the older Esposito sibling, Sebastiano, threatened a quickfire comeback two minutes later, forcing a sharp save from Mike Maignan.

Bradley Barcola came closest to a third goal before the break with a curling shot from the edge of the box that struck the foot of the far post.

The end-to-end nature of the game continued in the second half as Rayan Cherki’s rasping strike was tipped onto the post by Donnarumma before Italy charged up the other end and forced Maignan into a point-blank save from Cambiaghi.

Italy had a glorious chance to go in front when Cambiaghi was tripped by Malo Gusto to earn a penalty, but Sebastiano Esposito failed to join his brother on the scoresheet as he hammered his spot kick wide on the hour mark.

The Azzurri did not dwell on the disappointment for long, taking the lead just three minutes later when Frattesi drilled in a shot from a Federico Dimarco cross moments after the Inter Milan wing-back was brought off the bench.

Fellow substitute Antonio Vergara earned the home side another penalty when he was tripped by Dayot Upamecano, and this time Francesco Pio Esposito stepped up to drill a shot into the bottom corner.

The result continued a strong start to Roberto Mancini’s second spell as Italy coach as his side stretched their unbeaten run to four matches and notched their first home win over France since 1962.

Belgium host Italy and Turkiye travel to France in the final round of group games on Sunday.

Elsewhere, captain Harry Kane celebrated his record 126th cap for England with a match-winner from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday to qualify for the Nations League last eight.

The 33-year-old followed a script that seemed destined to happen when he stepped up in the 64th minute to put England ahead in front of an 80,400-strong crowd after the hosts had conceded a sloppy equaliser five minutes earlier.

It was the Bayern Munich forward’s 92nd England goal, and there was never any doubt from the moment he placed the ball and sent it straight down the middle as goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic dived to his left.

Kane had started a night of celebration as the centre of attention, handed a commemorative token by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, the previous record holder since 1989, when he surpassed Bobby Moore’s 108 caps.

articles.title: House passes bill to expand benefits for combat-injured veterans
articles.excerpt: The House approved legislation Thursday that would allow combat-injured military retirees with less than 20 years of service to collect their full military retirement pay and Department of Veterans Af...
articles.body_text:
The House approved legislation Thursday that would allow combat-injured military retirees with less than 20 years of service to collect their full military retirement pay and Department of Veterans Affairs disability compensation without the dollar-for-dollar offset that currently reduces their retirement benefits.

The passage of the Major Richard Star Act, H.R. 2102, sends the measure to the Senate, where lawmakers must still approve it before it can reach the president’s desk.

The vote followed a months-long effort led by Rep. Mark Takano, D-Calif., ranking Democrat on the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, to force consideration of the standalone legislation.

On May 21, Takano and Rep. Raul Ruiz, D-Calif., began an effort to force a House vote on a resolution that would set the rules for bringing the Major Richard Star Act to the floor. The petition reached the required 218 signatures on Sept. 15, with Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., providing the decisive endorsement.

On Thursday, lawmakers adopted H. Res. 1247 by a 271-135 vote, clearing the way for final consideration of the Star Act.

Rep. Joe Courtney, D-Conn., who signed the discharge petition, urged the Senate to act following Thursday’s passage.

“By finally passing the Major Richard Star Act, a bipartisan coalition just took a major step to follow through on that mission,” Courtney said in a Nov. 12 statement. He urged senators to send it to the president.

The bill’s Republican sponsor, Rep. Gus Bilirakis, R-Fla., introduced the legislation in 2020. Ruiz and Takano have been leading Democratic advocates for its passage.

Veterans of Foreign Wars National Commander-in-Chief Corey Geisler emphasized that securing a vote was not enough without passage of the full legislation.

“Getting a vote is not the finish line,” Geisler said. “Passing the right bill is.”

Following Thursday’s passage, Wounded Warrior Project applauded the House vote and called on the Senate to act.

“We thank House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano and Congressman Raul Ruiz for their efforts to advance the discharge petition, Congressman Gus Bilirakis for his longstanding commitment to the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act, and the members of the House of Representatives for taking an important step toward providing long-overdue relief for combat-injured veterans,” said Jose Ramos, the organization’s senior vice president of government and community relations.

The Senate companion, S. 1032, remains before the Senate Armed Services Committee. The Senate has no equivalent to the House discharge-petition process, and previous attempts to advance the measure by unanimous consent were blocked by objections. The Senate must still approve the legislation before it can be passed.

Natalie Oliverio is an independent journalist and Navy veteran who covers military and veterans’ issues. Drawing on her experience as a talent executive and mentor, she writes about the policies, people and programs shaping the military community.

articles.title: Angela Rayner grants planning approval for asylum centre in Piddington despite local opposition
articles.excerpt:
Home Office sign-off also needed for site that would house 1,200 asylum seekers near Oxfordshire village that voted to leave UK

The communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has approved full planning pe...
articles.body_text:
Home Office sign-off also needed for site that would house 1,200 asylum seekers near Oxfordshire village that voted to leave UK

The communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has approved full planning permission for an asylum centre at a Ministry of Defence site near the village of Piddington in Oxfordshire.

The decision approves plans to go ahead with the refurbishment and redevelopment of the former barracks. The Home Office insists that final approval is still to be determined.

In September, people in Piddington voted to leave the UK in a symbolic referendum against plans to house 1,256 detained asylum seekers nearby. A total of 285 people were in favour of independence from the UK while 26 voted against.

The poll was organised by campaigners for residents to demonstrate opposition to the plans for accommodation at the converted MoD site near the town of Bicester.

A Home Office spokesperson said on Thursday: “Planning permission allows us to continue to progress the use of MoD Bicester. However, a final decision to proceed is yet to be taken.

“The government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over £1bn saved in costs since the election.

“This includes closing all asylum hotels and moving to alternative accommodation, including former military sites. These are designed to be self-contained, with 24/7 security and CCTV, to minimise the impact on the local community.”

There is now a six-week window when the decision can face a legal challenge.

A Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government spokesperson said: “The secretary of state has granted full planning permission for the temporary, phased use of the former MoD Bicester storage site.

“As the decision may be subject to legal challenge, it would not be appropriate to comment further.”

Last month, campaigners against the government plans took their complaints to the high court.

The group Wrong Plan Wrong Site had appealed for a judicial review into the Home Office proposals for the former MoD Bicester site.

In August, the government concluded an environmental assessment was unnecessary for the proposed development.

But campaigners challenged that decision, with the group saying there were “credible concerns about potential significant environmental effects”.

Last summer Andy Burnham said that people in more affluent areas of the UK must “play their part” in housing asylum seekers.

Katie Lam, the shadow housing secretary of state, said: “Angela Rayner has told the people of Piddington that their voices count for nothing.

“A village of a few hundred people will now have 1,256 illegal male migrants housed on its doorstep against the wishes of almost everyone who lives there.

“Andy Burnham says every community must ‘play their part’ when it comes to housing illegal migrants, but why should British people suffer as a result of this government’s refusal to secure our border? The answer is not moving illegal migrants from hotels to military bases. It is removing them as soon as they arrive.

“Only the Conservatives are serious about protecting British communities.”

The Home Office announced in June it was exploring the use of three former military sites to house asylum seekers: MoD Bicester, MoD Barnham and MoD Linton-on-Ouse.

The government is also seeking to extend the use of two existing sites, Crowborough until 2030 and Wethersfield beyond 2027.

articles.title: Mamdani prepares to fulfill promise to axe NYPD unit responsible for controlling protest violence
articles.excerpt: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended his decision to retain NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite calls from the Democratic Socialists of America to remove her following an ICE-involved shoot...
articles.body_text:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended his decision to retain NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite calls from the Democratic Socialists of America to remove her following an ICE-involved shooting in the Bronx.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is reportedly preparing to announce his plan to disband the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), fulfilling a long-held campaign promise that has led to mounting pressure from his base, as well as questions about how the group's duties will be replaced.

Politico reported that Mamdani, a democratic socialist, is preparing to announce plans to disband the unit, which responds to protests, civil disturbances and major events while handling counterterrorism operations.

Mamdani has said he wants to decouple the unit’s protest and counterterrorism functions, but at a March City Council budget hearing Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said discussions with the mayor concerned "the future of how we police protests generally," not disbanding the unit.

MAMDANI IN HOT SEAT OVER POST MOURNING DEATH OF INMATE CHARGED WITH CALLOUS CRIME: 'ABSOLUTELTY SHAMEFUL'

NYPD Strategic Response Group (SRG) officers monitor a crowd outside 26 Federal Plaza on Oct. 21, 2025, in New York City. (Adam Gray/Getty Images)

The NYPD says the SRG responds to citywide mobilizations, civil disorders and major events and is a "critical asset" during parades, protests and the papal visit. SRG personnel are "also deployed to areas requiring an increased police presence due to increased crime or other conditions" and "mobilizes for shootings, bank robberies, missing persons, demonstrations, or other significant incidents," according to the department.

Tisch added during the March City Council budget hearing that the SRG does not typically deal with peaceful protests, but is deployed for protests that involve criminal activity. She also noted that in 2025 the NYPD facilitated 4,255 protests and the SRG was available at 245 of them, or roughly 6%.

Sources familiar with the plan told Politico that City Hall has been contemplating putting the SRG under Mamdani's new Office of Community Safety, launched earlier this year. The sources also said Mamdani's plan could be formalized via an executive order, according to Politico.

MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a news conference at Gracie Mansion alongside NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch on Monday, March 9, 2026. (Angelina Katsanis/AP)

"I've been clear that my vision is for the disbanding of the SRG. And the reason for that vision is that the SRG were created a little more than a decade ago with an intention first of dealing with threats, terroristic threats to the city," Mamdani said during a press conference in September.

"What it has eventually become is both dealing with counterterrorism and responses to exercising First Amendment rights," the mayor continued. "I do not believe that those purposes need to be dual purposes. I believe that we should have a focus on counterterrorism that is separate from our response to the use of First Amendment — [that] continues to be a conversation I'm having with our police commissioner."

Fox News Digital reached out to City Hall for confirmation and comment on the mayor's reported plan, but did not hear back in time for publication.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani attends a news conference at NYPD headquarters on Jan. 6, 2026, in New York City. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

"As the Mayor has said, our administration will disband the Strategic Response Group and separate protest response from counterterrorism," spokesperson Dora Pekec told Politico. "We will have more to share soon."

Fox News Digital reached out to the NYPD for comment.

Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

articles.title: ‘Win-win’ deal with EU could be done, Andy Burnham says
articles.excerpt:
Prime minister says reset could be a deal ‘like the Brexit people thought they were voting for in 2016’

Andy Burnham has said he believes a “win-win” deal could be done with the EU that could be “mor...
articles.body_text:
Prime minister says reset could be a deal ‘like the Brexit people thought they were voting for in 2016’

Andy Burnham has said he believes a “win-win” deal could be done with the EU that could be “more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016”.

The prime minister was meeting fellow leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin, ahead of a keenly anticipated EU-UK summit next week, where he hopes to bring Britain closer to Europe.

At the bilateral summit the EU and UK hope to sign deals on food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme, but the question of tuition fees for European students remains a stumbling block.

Burnham said: “I believe there is a good deal to be done that could be a win-win for Britain and Europe.

“The deal is not done, and there’ll be some long nights ahead in the next seven days.”

He said the reset would be about whether we can “take a step back to closer working relationships with Europe”.

Burnham added: “We ended up with a far harder Brexit, I think, than people thought they were getting when they went to the polls.”

The EU has said the prized food and drink deal and emissions-trading agreement may not enter into force without a deal on tuition fees in which European students would pay domestic rates.

Burnham said it was a package deal, but would not be drawn on whether he accepted the link. “I’m going to be fighting hard for these benefits for Britain in the next seven days … they will make a real difference. If I can do anything to address the cost of living crisis, I should be doing it.”

He has previously said the food and drink deal, which will ease Brexit red tape, will add 0.4% to British GDP.

The prime minister also said David Cameron had been wrong to argue that Britain’s problems had “nothing to do with Brexit”, adding there would be “long nights ahead” to negotiate a reset with the EU before the summit.

Cameron, the prime minister who lost the 2016 Brexit referendum, told Bloomberg News that Burnham should not seek to bring Britain back into the EU, arguing that the UK’s problems had nothing to do with its exit from the EU.

Asked about those remarks, Burnham said: “I think he is wrong to say that the low growth that we’ve had over the last decade has, quote, ‘nothing to do with Brexit’. I would say the evidence says otherwise.

“It feels like his intervention is more about unity in the Conservative party than it is about fighting for the British interests.”

Burnham has recently said he is open to rejoining the single market, customs union or to “go all the way” by rejoining the EU. He said a deeper relationship would be the outcome of future talks “and it will be in the outcome of that negotiation that then we will take a decision as a cabinet, on what, if anything, comes next”.

Earlier on Thursday, the EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, said she wanted to see Britain rejoin the EU, but warned that negotiations would not be easy after the “trauma” of the Brexit years.

She said: “I would very much like to see Britain back in Europe, but, of course, we also have in the European Union, a lot of, I would say, trauma from Britain leaving, so the negotiations will not be that easy.”

Burnham is expected to make the EU reset the centrepiece of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet on Monday night – though it will range widely across foreign policy challenges.

No 10 sources said the speech would be focused on the upcoming Brussels summit – and look ahead to the next stage in 2027 – rather than outline what a more permanent close relationship might look like.

Officials at the UK-EU summit will also discuss the agenda for the next round of the reset, expected to focus on a joint migration pact.

It could also target collaboration on law enforcement and borders, visas for touring artists, and mutual recognition of qualifications.

Ministry of Justice officials are also trying to water down an EU ultimatum on halting the deportation of foreign national offenders. “This is the classic wheeze that the EU always pulls at the last minute of negotiations,” one Whitehall source said.

The next week is expected to be fraught with last-minute negotiations. Key will be access to Made in Europe, which has the potential to lock British firms out of continental supply chains and public contracts if no deal is done.

Negotiations could be challenging despite the lure of the UK making a potential concession on tuition fees in exchange for inclusion in the Made in Europe legislation.

The EU has long said there cannot be a deal on Made in Europe at the summit, because it has yet to finalise its own position.

The joint communique for 2027 is expected to call for strengthening efforts between the UK and the most exposed member states to the small boats crisis in the Channel.

This will centre on both the EU’s Channel action plan, already in place since June this year, and a possible framework for a wider bespoke EU-UK migration plan.

The UK is believed to be pushing for access to the Eurodac database, which carries the fingerprints of asylum seekers, as well as to the Schengen Information System (SIS), which records details on fugitives, missing people and stolen goods.

The UK was the third biggest user of SIS before it lost access through Brexit.

articles.title: China rules out hosting Cop33 climate summit in 2028
articles.excerpt:
Decision disappoints experts hoping for world’s biggest emitter to take global lead on climate crisis

China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, le...
articles.body_text:
Decision disappoints experts hoping for world’s biggest emitter to take global lead on climate crisis

China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, leaving the field open for other Asian countries to hold it, the Guardian understands.

The decision will disappoint many countries and climate experts, who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would take the lead on the global stage, as the US under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international cooperation on the climate.

Al Gore, the former US vice-president, was among those left disheartened by the decision. “I would be very much in favour of that idea [of China hosting the summit],” he told the Guardian. “It’s too bad.”

China is in the midst of an economic transformation, from being heavily dependent on coal to becoming an “electro state”. John Kerry, the former US secretary of state, told the Guardian that China was leaving the rest of the world behind in forging and using the low-carbon technologies of the future.

Renewable energy generation capacity has now outstripped coal in China, and its greenhouse gas emissions appear to have declined slightly this year.

Sales of electric vehicles in the country have also taken off, making up nearly two-thirds of the market last month, and China’s clean energy industries drove more than 90% of the country’s investment growth last year.

The rules of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) mean an Asian country should host in 2028.

Gareth Redmond-King, the international lead at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit thinktank, said China’s position as an industrial powerhouse would have made it a formidable contender to hold the summit.

“It would undoubtedly be significant for the world’s biggest emitter and second-biggest economy to host a climate Cop,” he said.

“They’re leading the world on investment, manufacture and deployment of clean energy tech, and their emissions have started to tick down. As a leadership story, China hosting Cop33 would be a big deal.”

It is not clear why China has decided against hosting the conference, but several experts that spoke to the Guardian suggested that the US electoral cycle was likely to have been a factor. The next US presidential election will take place on 7 November 2028, and Cop33 is scheduled for 6 to 17 November that year.

After the strong showing by Democrats in the recent midterm elections, in which voter concern over the climate crisis was thought to be a factor, the Democrats will be hoping to elect a climate-friendly president in 2028. But even if they succeed, Trump will still be in office until the following January.

The US president rejects climate science and withdrew the US from the Paris agreement, and is also withdrawing from its parent treaty, the 1992 UNFCCC.

China seeks to be seen as a leader among developing countries, but has been wary of stepping into the gap left by the US. Under the Democratic presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama, the US and China enjoyed a close partnership on climate issues, setting joint targets on reducing methane and developing clean technology.

Cop33 will be an important meeting because it will include the “global stocktake” – a mechanism under the 2015 Paris climate agreement that examines countries’ progress on cutting emissions in line with the goal of limiting global temperature rises to 1.5C.

That limit is now certain to be surpassed, but experts say countries should now try to minimise the temperature “overshoot”, to avoid worse ravages from extreme weather.

India’s government considered offering to host Cop33 for several months earlier this year, but also decided against it. India’s coal use has been increasing, even as the country exceeds its own renewable energy targets.

The Guardian understands that other countries mulling a bid to host Cop33 include Uzbekistan, South Korea, Indonesia and Thailand.

No decision on a host is likely to be made at this year’s Cop31 meeting, which is ongoing in Turkey, with the Turkish and Australian governments jointly presiding over the summit.

articles.title: Pentagon backs war memorial guard who reprimanded Hegseth's group
articles.excerpt:
US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery.

The Pentagon has given its backing to a US Army guard who reprimanded a group that inclu...
articles.body_text:
US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery.

The Pentagon has given its backing to a US Army guard who reprimanded a group that included US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Arlington National Cemetery.

A video of the Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

The footage showed the army sentinel on duty stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum."

"The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored - and will always honor - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe."

On Thursday, he presented an award to the soldier who reprimanded his group.

Hegseth "welcomed the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, the Old Guard to the Pentagon where he proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026," the Pentagon said in a statement.

In a post on X showing the soldier, Hesgeth said: "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist."

The Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct.

The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I.

A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948.

It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and First Lady Melania Trump bow their heads in prayer during a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery

Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery.

During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war.

"Under this administration, and it was about time, somebody fought back. All of us fought back," he said.

"And we won," Trump said of the Iran war. "It's just a question of when we want to end it. We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory."

Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary.

Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth amid Democratic lawmakers' push to impeach him. On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill.

Hegseth has called the impeachment efforts a "farce" and a "stunt".

articles.title: Finland says it detects strike on Russian warship in Baltic Sea
articles.excerpt:
HELSINKI — Finland’s military said on Thursday its forces had detected “a strike” on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea a day earlier, but that the security situation in the area remained stable.

It...
articles.body_text:
HELSINKI — Finland’s military said on Thursday its forces had detected “a strike” on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea a day earlier, but that the security situation in the area remained stable.

It was not immediately clear if there were any casualties or what had caused the strike. Estonian media reported on Thursday that the vessel was a small Russian navy ship and that it later returned to St. Petersburg.

“The Finnish Defence Forces detected… a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation,” a spokesperson for the Nordic country’s military said in an emailed statement to Reuters.

Finland is not under any immediate military threat, the spokesperson added. The defense forces declined to provide further details about the location or timing of the incident, or how it was detected.

Ukraine has been sending waves of military drones towards Russia’s northwest Leningrad region, which includes the city of St. Petersburg as well as the Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, a major export outlet for commodities such as oil and grain.

Some Ukrainian drones have strayed into the airspace of Finland and the Baltic region, leading to fears that the war is spilling over into NATO countries that border Russia and its ally Belarus.

Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania early on Wednesday issued warnings to citizens to take shelter due to drones in their airspace, and NATO scrambled warplanes in response.

The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia that extends eastwards to St Petersburg.

articles.title: Spain approves housing reforms after nationwide strike over costs
articles.excerpt: The Spanish parliament has passed measures to limit evictions and real estate speculation in an attempt to make housing more affordable, a day after a nationwide general strike over the country’s hous...
articles.body_text:
The Spanish parliament has passed measures to limit evictions and real estate speculation in an attempt to make housing more affordable, a day after a nationwide general strike over the country’s housing crisis.

Spain’s interim lower house of parliament ratified the housing measures on Thursday; however, their duration will depend on the outcome of a snap election scheduled later in November.

The leading opposition party, the conservative Popular Party, has said that it will repeal the measures of the left-wing government if it takes power, which polls indicate could happen.

Large demonstrations over unaffordable housing swept the country in September when televised images of the eviction of 87-year-old Maria del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, from her home, shocked many Spaniards.

Protest camps sprang up in several cities, the largest in Madrid’s emblematic Puerta del Sol square. Maricarmen’s subsequent death in October caused national uproar, prompting Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s minority government to rush to present two decrees.

Sanchez called the general election, which had been scheduled for 2027, in response to the parliament’s failure to pass the decrees that included greater protection for tenants against evictions and the automatic renewal of tenant contracts.

The Popular Party and other conservative parties aligned to reject the measures, saying the laws would negatively affect the housing market, and proposed a building spree as the solution to the crisis.

On Wednesday, hundreds of thousands of Spaniards took to the streets in a 24-hour walkout over soaring rents and the high cost of living that the main unions called after the decrees were blocked.

Sanchez introduced another two decrees that were almost identical to the rejected ones. They were presented to a smaller parliamentary council on Thursday, giving the government a better chance of passing the laws.

The first decree passed in a 35–34 vote and includes a measure extending protections against evictions for tenants deemed by social services to be in a precarious financial or social position, as long as regional authorities cannot offer them an alternative residence.

Another measure attempted to reduce real estate speculation by stopping any company involved in the real estate market from buying properties for less than 70 percent of their value.

However, it was rejected 34-35 after the centre-right Basque party voted with the right-wing bloc after having supported the other decree, on grounds that the measure could lead homeowners to withdraw their properties from the rental market, triggering a drop in supply and even higher prices.

articles.title: Eight killed in Colombian air strike targeting Gulf Clan gang
articles.excerpt:
Colombia's president said one of 10 "priority targets" was among those killed

A senior leader of Colombia's largest criminal gang, the Gulf Clan, is among eight people killed in an air strike carried...
articles.body_text:
Colombia's president said one of 10 "priority targets" was among those killed

A senior leader of Colombia's largest criminal gang, the Gulf Clan, is among eight people killed in an air strike carried out by the country's armed forces, according to President Abelardo de la Espriella.

De la Espriella said he had personally authorised the bombing targeting the Gulf Clan in the province of Antioquia, in north-west Colombia.

He added that Haminton Mosquera, whom he described as a senior member of the crime gang and one of 10 "priority targets" for Colombia's security forces, had been "brought down".

De la Espriella was elected in June after campaigning on a promise to crack down on Colombia's powerful criminal gangs, including by launching air strikes.

In a post on X, external, he said that Mosquera was suspected of having ordered attacks against the security forces, including the murder of a police officer in the municipality of Tarazá last year.

The Gulf Clan has been engaging in criminal activities for decades, mainly trafficking cocaine from Colombia to destinations in the US and Europe but also  illegal mining and people smuggling.

The US added it to its list of Foreign Terrorist Organisations (FTOs) last year.

In his post, President de la Espriella said that "the offensive won't stop" and vowed to regain control of areas currently controlled by criminal organisations such as the Gulf Clan.

While his offensive against criminal gangs has been welcomed by many living in areas where extortion and gang violence are rampant, de la Espriella has faced criticism for the way he has made some of his announcements on security.

Less than a month after taking office, he published a video showing him walking among 23 body bags containing the remains of 23 people killed in an air strike on a suspected guerrilla camp.

On Wednesday, he shared a photo, external in which he can be seen writing his campaign slogan, "Welcome to the miracle homeland" on a bomb.

He has also defended his decision to wear an army uniform at a recent event in Cúcuta at which he confronted a detainee suspected of being a Farc rebel.

"What did you make of the bomb I sent you, signed by me?," the president can be heard asking the man.

He later told journalists that he wore the uniform because "I am a soldier of the homeland. That's why I dress like a soldier, because I came to serve Colombia. Because I honour the heroes, police officers and military."

Additional reporting by BBC Monitoring's Luis Fajardo.

Colombia's new president loosens gun control rules

Alleged rebel leader killed in Colombia as president targets armed groups

US offers $1bn to Colombia on new right-wing president's first day of office

articles.title: Suspected bomb hoax threats force fresh evacuations of Italian schools
articles.excerpt:
Bomb squads have searched many schools but no devices have been found

Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations.

Some 1,800 sc...
articles.body_text:
Bomb squads have searched many schools but no devices have been found

Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations.

Some 1,800 schools, from Milan in the north to Sicily in the south, reported receiving a similar threat to one that created chaos in Italy on Wednesday - even though no devices have been found anywhere.

The Italian government has advised schools that "in the absence of concrete evidence beyond the simple receipt of a mass email indicating a danger, buildings must not not be evacuated".

Schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland received threats on Wednesday, too. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

On Thursday morning, a bomb alert at a Calais rail station delayed international and national train services in northern France.

The latest incidents follow a series of bomb hoaxes last week against airports and airlines in a number of European countries.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

Wednesday's email threat - sent to 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 Italian state schools   - was said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan".

Some officials say it originated in Taiwan.

A similar message sent to Italian schools on Thursday, again signed by Mikhail Andropov, is said to have been sent from the account of a teacher in the Philippines whose account is believed to have been hacked.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has spoken of "a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern".

No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister

Police treating threatening email sent to more than 300 schools as 'hoax'

Many parents, though, are concerned and have been demanding clarity and action from the government.

La Repubblica newspaper reports that protests have been held against a decision by the headmaster of a secondary school in Rome who did not take any action, saying she had realised the threatening message to contain typos and therefore be "fake".

According to the newspaper, protesters want new national guidelines to be issued.

Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats

articles.title: Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in Gaza kills surgeon and five others
articles.excerpt:
Hospital director says 28 wounded in attack on one of few remaining medical facilities in the strip

An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and...
articles.body_text:
Hospital director says 28 wounded in attack on one of few remaining medical facilities in the strip

An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.

The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence.

The strike destroyed part of the surgery department, and caused extensive damage to several floors. Services were suspended in four departments: radiology, laboratories, surgical operations and inpatient surgical wards, according to Dr Ahmed al-Fara, hospital director.

The ceiling of one of the wards had caved in, while debris-covered beds lay next to medical instruments twisted from the force of the blast. In other rooms, piles of rubble and shattered concrete cluttered the floor and a hole was left in the floor, where the bomb penetrated the building.

Dr Ayman Abu Ubaid, a surgical specialist at Nasser medical complex, who was wounded in the attack, said: “The bombing caused thick smoke to fill the rooms and fires to break out, amid the groans of wounded and people’s screams. There were many casualties and blood everywhere … Most of us sustained injuries to our limbs, as well as shrapnel wounds in different parts of our bodies.”

Ubaid said the strike came at about 12.30am, without warning. “The patients in the department were all surgical patients waiting to undergo operations. The bombing happened at a time when they should have been asleep,” he said.

Among the dead was Rizk Abu Shaira, 52, a general surgeon who had featured in American Doctor, a documentary about doctors operating in Gaza.

“Dr Rizk was in the American Doctor documentary operating and serving his people. He lost his life doing that, he lost his life because he was doing that,” Dr Thaer Ahmad, who also featured in the documentary, posted on X.

Abu Shaira was killed alongside one of his patients, on whom he had operated.

Nasser hospital is one of the last functioning healthcare facilities in Gaza, after Israeli bombing made most of the strip’s facilities unusable. Last year Israel also struck the hospital, killing five journalists in a double-tap strike on a location often used by reporters for filming. In all, the hospital has been attacked seven times since the war on Gaza began.

The Israeli military has accused Hamas of using hospitals as command centres and to store weapons, an accusation the militant movement rejects. More than 1,700 healthcare workers have been killed in Gaza, while Doctors Without Borders (MSF) says Israel has detained hundreds of medics since 7 October 2023, with at least 95 still in custody.

About 90% of Gaza’s health infrastructure has been destroyed or damage by Israeli bombing, systematic destruction UN experts called “medicide”.

Attacking healthcare facilities and staff is illegal under international humanitarian law, though these facilities can lose their protected status if they are used for military purposes.

There is an increased need for healthcare during the winter months in Gaza, where rains have displaced people from their tents and increased communicable diseases in crowded encampments.

Already, Nasser hospital is lacking about 80% of its essential medicines and medical supplies, said al-Fara, its director.

One of those killed in Thursday’s strike was Seif Ghazi Abu Hatab, 29, who was admitted to Nasser hospital on Monday after a piece of debris fell on his back while he was helping clear rubble from a friend’s home. He was scheduled for surgery at 10am on Thursday, and was meant to receive further treatment abroad.

“Seif was a young man in the prime of his life. He wanted to live, rebuild his home and start a normal life, free from problems and suffering … Seif was killed after already losing two of his brothers and his father. His mother has now lost three of her sons,” said his cousin Tareq Abu Hatab, 37.

Israel launched the war in Gaza after the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack that killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostage. At least 74,645 people have since been killed in Gaza and Israel has carried out a genocide in the strip, according to the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory.

Israel continues to carry out airstrikes in Gaza, killing more than 1,600 people since the October 2025 “ceasefire”, according to the Gaza ministry of health.

articles.title: Trump asks Vance to focus on ‘corruption and crime’ in Dem-run cities, states
articles.excerpt: Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy joins ‘America Reports’ to detail the Trump administration’s nationwide push to crack down on SNAP fraud. Federal prosecutors have uncovered more ...
articles.body_text:
Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy joins ‘America Reports’ to detail the Trump administration’s nationwide push to crack down on SNAP fraud. Federal prosecutors have uncovered more than $42 million in stolen funds as officials ramp up efforts to identify fraud across the country.

President Donald Trump said Thursday that he has asked Vice President JD Vance to focus his "complete and total attention" on alleged widespread corruption and crime in Democrat-led cities and states, accusing blue state leaders of allowing billions of dollars to be stolen each month.

In a Truth Social post, Trump singled out Minnesota, California and Illinois as examples of states he claims are plagued by corruption and mismanagement, arguing that cracking down on the alleged criminal activity could help balance the federal budget.

"I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.," Trump wrote.

JD VANCE WARNS BLUE STATE OFFICIALS COULD FACE PRISON OVER BILLION-DOLLAR FRAUD EPIDEMIC

President Donald Trump speaks before signing an executive order regarding a task force on fraud in the Oval Office of the White House, Monday, March 16, 2026, in Washington, as Vice President JD Vance listens. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

"The Blue States, such as Minnesota, California, Illinois, and many more, are all poorly run, corrupt disasters," he continued. "Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month."

Trump did not provide specific examples in his post of how billions of dollars are allegedly being stolen each month.

Vance already leads the White House's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, which Trump established through a March 16 executive order aimed at combating fraud, waste and abuse in federally funded benefit programs.

The task force is charged with coordinating federal efforts to strengthen eligibility verification, prevent improper payments and identify suspected fraud in government benefit programs.

WALZ ADMINISTRATION IGNORED FRAUD WARNINGS AS BILLIONS VANISHED, HOUSE OVERSIGHT REPORT ALLEGES

The executive order also identified Minnesota, California and Illinois among states where the administration alleged widespread fraud or vulnerabilities in government benefit programs.

In October, Fox News Digital reported that the Vance-led task force was preparing to announce criminal charges against more than 40 defendants in an alleged $40 million Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme.

At the time, the task force reported identifying $260.7 billion in suspected fraud since Trump took office and preventing an estimated $72 billion in potentially fraudulent payments on an annualized basis. Those figures have not been independently verified.

It was not immediately clear whether Trump's latest directive would expand Vance's existing responsibilities or signal a renewed emphasis on investigating alleged corruption in Democratic-led jurisdictions.

President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during the 157th National Memorial Day Observance at Arlington National Cemetery, Monday, May 26, 2025, in Arlington, Va. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and Department of Justice for comment on the president's directive and the allegations of widespread fraud.

Trump also suggested that eliminating the alleged corruption could help balance the federal budget.

VANCE-LED TASK FORCE CUTS OFF $1.4B FROM HOME HEALTH, HOSPICE PROVIDERS SUSPECTED OF FRAUD

"Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large scale criminal activity," Trump wrote, before adding, "CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s blood!"

The president did not explain how eliminating the alleged corruption would balance the federal budget.

President Donald Trump speaks in the James Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Washington, D.C.

Trump then pivoted to Iran, declaring that the United States no longer needs to negotiate a deal with Tehran.

"We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote. "We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!"

Trump did not elaborate on his claims regarding Iranian funds or the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically important waterway for global energy shipments.

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for clarification on the president's remarks regarding Iran.
