articles.title: More than one million people in Lebanon face acute food shortages, UN says
articles.excerpt: Nearly a quarter of Lebanon’s population, or more than one million people, is facing acute food shortages due to two consecutive conflicts in less than two years and a dire economic situation, accordi...
articles.body_text:
Nearly a quarter of Lebanon’s population, or more than one million people, is facing acute food shortages due to two consecutive conflicts in less than two years and a dire economic situation, according to the United Nations.

The UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization, the World Food Programme (WFP) and Lebanon’s Ministry of Agriculture warned in a joint statement published on Wednesday that the number is expected to rise to 1.15 million by the middle of next year.

“Employment opportunities remain limited, savings have been depleted, and debt remains high, while the cost of food, fuel and other essentials continues to strain household budgets,” the joint statement said.

“Some households can still draw on savings, borrow, cut expenses or find other ways to put food on the table. For others, those options are being exhausted. When families have nothing left to fall back on, even a small additional shock can push them deeper into crisis,” Allison Oman Lawi, WFP representative and country director in Lebanon, said.

Lebanon’s Agriculture Minister Nizar Hani said: “These findings call for a coordinated national response that addresses urgent food needs while protecting livelihoods and restoring productive capacity.”

Lebanon’s authorities estimate that the cost of two wars between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah since October 2023 amounts to about $27bn.

The last war, launched in March, displaced more than one million people in Lebanon. That number has fallen to about 300,000 since violence subsided in June.

Despite a United States-brokered framework deal signed between Israel and Lebanon’s government in June to bring fighting to an end, Israel is still occupying land in Lebanon.

Under the terms, Israeli forces were to withdraw, and Lebanon’s army was to take up positions in vacated territory.

Lebanon was meant to disarm Hezbollah, which is not a party to the agreement.

The fighting broke out as Lebanon struggled to recover from its worst-ever economic crisis, which began in 2019.

Beirut has been seeking a bailout from the International Monetary Fund but has yet to implement reforms demanded by the institution to release the aid.

articles.title: Will Sheikh Hasina return to Bangladesh?
articles.excerpt:
The former Bangladeshi PM says she is planning to go back, despite a death sentence.

She faces being hanged. Yet, Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Bangladesh and would rather die in her country....
articles.body_text:
The former Bangladeshi PM says she is planning to go back, despite a death sentence.

She faces being hanged. Yet, Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Bangladesh and would rather die in her country.

She served twice as prime minister, but was forced to resign and flee after large-scale street protests more than two years ago.

Since then, she has been living in India, which has refused a request by Bangladesh to hand her over.

Hasina says she asked for a new passport to return. But the government in Dhaka turned down the request.

The former leader announced she will return home in December, no matter what.

So, what would her possible return mean for politics in Bangladesh?

Shahab Enam Khan – Professor at the Department of International Relations at Jahangirnagar University

Sanjay Kumar Bhardwaj – Professor at the Centre for South Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, specialising in India-Bangladesh relations

Taqbir Huda – Human rights lawyer and a Clarendon scholar at the University of Oxford

articles.title: Watch: Vinícius Jr's surprise message to boy who received prosthetic legs after Sudan drone strike
articles.excerpt:
Real Madrid footballer Vinícius Júnior has sent a surprise video message to 13-year-old Zaher praising his courage and inviting him to spend the day together at a Real Madrid game.

Zaher lost both hi...
articles.body_text:
Real Madrid footballer Vinícius Júnior has sent a surprise video message to 13-year-old Zaher praising his courage and inviting him to spend the day together at a Real Madrid game.

Zaher lost both his legs after a drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan, where the battle between Sudan's army and the RSF continues to devastate the country.

When the BBC first met him in 2025 he said that he dreamt of being able to walk and play football again. His story resonated with viewers and money was raised for treatment in Cairo, including prosthetic legs.

After surgery followed by months of physiotherapy and psychological support in Cairo, Zehar returned to Sudan feeling "uplifted" by Vini Jr's message he says.

articles.title: Spain’s first general strike in 14 years begins
articles.excerpt:
Millions of workers across Spain are striking to demand government action over the country’s housing crisis, less than three weeks before a national election that could bring the far right to power.

...
articles.body_text:
Millions of workers across Spain are striking to demand government action over the country’s housing crisis, less than three weeks before a national election that could bring the far right to power.

The 24-hour walkout, which began at midnight on Wednesday, disrupted public transport and forced businesses, factories and shops to scale back operations or close entirely across the eurozone’s fourth-largest economy. It’s Spain’s first general strike in 14 years.

Minor incidents were reported in the first hours, including roadblocks with burning tyres in Barcelona, the second-largest city in the country. There were also scuffles between picketers and police near the country’s main wholesale market on the outskirts of the capital, Madrid.

The two main unions that called the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors”, including 90 percent in the automotive and port sectors, according to a statement posted on social media.

The CEOE organisation, which represents business leaders, said in a statement that the impact varied by region and area of work, with a “low participation” in most sectors.

The UGT and CCOO unions called the strike following a wave of nationwide protests over access to housing, sparked by the eviction in September of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old Madrid pensioner who died several days later.

The demonstrations included a five-week occupation of Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol square, where hundreds of tents were pitched, sparking imitations in other cities.

The average rent in Spain has almost doubled over the past 10 years, eating into household budgets and angering voters.

Spain’s socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap election for November 29 after his minority government failed to secure parliamentary approval for a package of housing measures proposed in response to the protests.

“This is not a strike against anyone, but rather one in favour of a common response from all levels of government to a real problem, which is access to housing,” he said in an interview published Sunday in the daily newspaper La Vanguardia.

The strike has been rejected by business groups, which have described it as an election-related protest, and criticised by the conservative opposition Popular Party (PP) and far-right Vox.

PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo warned that unions risked being linked to Sanchez “forever” if they went ahead with the strike in the run-up to the election.

Feijoo, whose party leads opinion polls, said going ahead with the strike was a “serious mistake” following a high-speed train collision last month in central Spain that killed 69 people.

Spain’s average gross monthly salary is about 2,460 euros, while renting a 50-square-metre apartment in Madrid cost an average of 1,170 euros a month in October, according to property portal Idealista.

That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, and 98.7 percent of the average young person’s income, according to the Youth Council of Spain. It’s well above the 30 percent share commonly recommended by housing experts and public institutions.

articles.title: Veterans Day 2026 brings free meals at popular restaurants — and some deals don't end Nov. 11
articles.excerpt: Alison Quinn, president of Dinova, tells Fox News Digital how participating restaurants are showing appreciation for America's military community through complimentary menu items and promotional offer...
articles.body_text:
Alison Quinn, president of Dinova, tells Fox News Digital how participating restaurants are showing appreciation for America's military community through complimentary menu items and promotional offers, including incentives for future visits.

Veterans and active-duty military members can find free food and other promotions at restaurants across the country on Veterans Day, Nov. 11. Some offers also give customers a reason to return for another deal later.

About 30 restaurant brands are included in Dinova's 2026 Veterans Day Dining Guide, according to Alison Quinn, the company's Florida-based president.

The guide is in its fifth year and includes national and regional chains like Bonefish Grill, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Hooters, Outback Steakhouse and Red Lobster.

102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115'

"What we're starting to see now is it's going beyond Veterans Day, to try to give back to the vets in a way that is more meaningful," Quinn told Fox News Digital. "Just not about one day but come back, and we'll give you something again."

Quinn pointed to California-based Hofman Hospitality Group, which is offering select meals to veterans and a $10 bonus card for a future visit. Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que is among the group's brands.

The Veterans Day Dining Guide is a compilation of restaurants offering free meals and discounts to veterans and active-duty military. (iStock)

Outback Steakhouse is offering a complimentary Bloomin' Onion and soft drink, along with a meal offer for a return visit, she said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Other deals listed in the guide include 10 free boneless wings and fries at Buffalo Wild Wings, a complimentary Red's Big Tavern Burger at Red Robin, free shrimp at Red Lobster and a free All-American Smash at Smashburger.

Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que is among the restaurants offering certain meals for free to veterans on Nov. 11. (Noah Graham/NBAE via Getty Images)

Dinova started the guide to share offers with veterans and, in some cases, active-duty military personnel, Quinn said. The company's business dining network includes about 25,000 restaurants and 600 corporate partners, she said.

Downloads of the guide have increased over the years, Quinn said, and the promotions may be useful for veterans or active-duty personnel who are struggling or "living under a tight budget."

The Bloomin' Onion is a popular Outback Steakhouse appetizer that is free for veterans on Nov. 11. (Oliver Tsang/South China Morning Post via Getty Images)

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Asked which deal she would choose, Quinn singled out Eddie Merlot's complimentary cheeseburger. Her father is an 85-year-old veteran, she said, and she plans to tell him about it.

Veterans and active-duty military members should bring identification and check with their local restaurant before visiting, Quinn said. Participation and ID requirements can vary by location and offer.

Peter Burke is a lifestyle editor with Fox News Digital. He covers various lifestyle topics, with an emphasis on food and drink.

articles.title: Washington AG's office indicates it will defend girls' sports ballot measure after ACLU sues to block it
articles.excerpt:
Seattle’s school board unanimously authorized potential legal action Monday against a voter-approved measure barring biological males from girls’ school sports. (Credit: Seattle Public Schools)

Washi...
articles.body_text:
Seattle’s school board unanimously authorized potential legal action Monday against a voter-approved measure barring biological males from girls’ school sports. (Credit: Seattle Public Schools)

Washington Attorney General Nick Brown’s office indicated it will fight to uphold a new voter-approved measure barring biological males from girls’ school sports, after the ACLU of Washington and other groups announced a lawsuit to block the measure.

"When a new law is passed by the people or the Legislature, our role is to ensure it is defended regardless of our personal views about the policy. We will review court filings as they come and discuss next steps," Brown’s office told OutKick.

However, the lawsuit to challenge the initiative involves Brown’s former law firm, a teachers union that supported his campaign and the former employer of his policy director. His office reiterated its position when OutKick asked follow-up questions about those connections and how the defense would be handled.

JACKSON THOMPSON: WASHINGTON STATE DEMOCRATIC PARTY CALLS GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE UNCONSTITUTIONAL

Supporters of Initiative 638, a Nov. 3 ballot measure in Washington state that would require K-12 athletes to compete according to their sex at birth speak at a pre-meet rally.  (OutKick)

"We’re discussing next steps and do not have more to add to the previous comment at this time. Again, when a new law is passed by the people or the Legislature, our role is to ensure it is defended regardless of our personal views about the policy," the office said.

The responses did not identify who would lead the defense or say whether the office had evaluated recusal or screening measures concerning those relationships.

Pacifica Law Group, where Brown previously served as a partner, is representing the Washington Education Association in the challenge, according to the Northwest Progressive Institute’s account of the filing.

Brown worked as a Pacifica partner from 2017 to 2021 before accepting President Joe Biden’s appointment as U.S. attorney for Western Washington, according to the firm. He returned in June 2023, and Pacifica identified him as a partner when it announced his election as attorney general in November 2024.

The Washington Education Association endorsed Brown’s 2024 campaign, according to Transparency USA.

The union’s political action committee was also among Brown’s campaign donors, according to The Spokesman-Review’s 2024 candidate profile, which cited Washington Public Disclosure Commission information. The profile did not specify the contribution amount.

Brown’s policy director, Enoka Herat, previously served as the ACLU of Washington’s policing and immigration policy program director.

Brown, a Democrat, also has a record of supporting transgender students’ participation in girls’ sports.

On Oct. 31, 2025, he led a coalition of attorneys general in filing an amicus brief supporting Minnesota’s policy in Female Athletes United v. Keith Ellison. The coalition urged the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to deny an emergency injunction that would have barred transgender students from most girls’ sports.

"I believe strongly in protecting the rights of all Washington kids—including transgender youth," Brown said in his office’s announcement of that amicus brief.

JACKSON THOMPSON: SEATTLE SCHOOL BOARD AUTHORIZES LEGAL CHALLENGE TO BALLOT MEASURE PROTECTING GIRLS' SPORTS

He argued that sports participation benefits children’s physical and emotional well-being and that excluding students based on gender identity perpetuates discrimination.

The lawsuit challenging Washington’s initiative was filed Monday in King County Superior Court. Plaintiffs include TransFamilies, the Washington Education Association and parents of transgender and nontransgender students who participate in girls’ sports.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The challengers argue the initiative violates state constitutional privacy protections and anti-discrimination law.

"Initiative 638 seeks to deny transgender girls equal opportunities simply because of who they are. It is discrimination, and it threatens all girls who play sports at school," the ACLU said in its announcement.

Let’s Go Washington, the organization behind the initiative, disputed the lawsuit’s claims Tuesday and argued existing sports physicals could satisfy the medical verification requirement.

Brown’s office also said it does not serve as legal counsel to the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association or local school districts.

"We don’t speculate on hypothetical events. Also, we only provide legal guidance to our state agency clients, which do not include WIAA or local school districts. We advise the state Office of the Superintendent of Public Instruction, and any such conversations would be attorney-client privileged," the office said.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Romanian servers targeted by Russian hackers to scoop up emails about NATO, EU
articles.excerpt: VIENNA — Hackers linked to Russia’s FSB quietly compromised a Romanian government organization’s servers to collect emails related to NATO and the EU in December 2025, a Slovak cybersecurity firm has ...
articles.body_text:
VIENNA — Hackers linked to Russia’s FSB quietly compromised a Romanian government organization’s servers to collect emails related to NATO and the EU in December 2025, a Slovak cybersecurity firm has revealed.

Using an advanced suite of tools that the researchers dubbed Cereal, a pun on the technology of serialization, emails going through Romanian government servers were scanned for a relation to NATO and the European Union. If this was discovered, the malicious software would create a copy for its Russian spymasters.

In particular, one component, CerealBox, targeted messages involving NATO and EU institutional addresses, the cybersecurity form ESET said. The module selected emails with Word or PDF attachments using predefined filters, then compressed and encrypted copies for later retrieval by the attackers.

The hack was discovered by the Bratislava-based  company and made public on Nov. 10. ESET had first discovered the tool being used against Kazakhstan in November 2025, and found the infiltration of Romania’s Microsoft Exchange servers a month later.

In a blog post and press release, the company attributed the attack to the known hacking group Turla, which it said was generally considered to be affiliated with Russia’s FSB, the country’s domestic intelligence agency. Turla has also been involved in attacks against high-profile Ukrainian targets, and the researchers said 70% of countries the group targeted were post-Soviet or post-communist states in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. The APT – a term designating an “Advanced Persistent Threat,” or known hacking group – primarily attacks government institutions.

ESET attributed the toolset to Turla with high confidence, citing the simultaneous use of another component publicly linked to the group and conceptual similarities to older Turla malware.

The researchers also noted a surge in activity in Kazakhstan on Jan. 15, 2026, the day after Old New Year, an informal holiday observed in Russia and some neighboring countries. “While malware does not celebrate holidays, its operators do,” the company wrote.

Romanian servers were compromised on Dec. 23, 2025, ESET researchers said; roughly a month after the cybersecurity firm first detected the same malicious code on the server of a Kazakh government agency. That discovery was the first time this tool had been seen, which the researchers described as “a previously undocumented toolset: a collection of modular .NET malware designed to run on Microsoft Exchange servers, receive commands, execute them in memory, map the compromised organization, and collect selected email messages.”

The tool was unusual for its “combination of novel techniques requiring deep knowledge of Exchange internals with unusual .NET execution methods,” ESET wrote.

The tool was designed to be especially stealthy, meant to allow it to spy undetected at length. While malware commonly communicates with an external command-and-control server, which can lead to detection and help cybersecurity professionals trace the origin, Cereal used the target organization’s own Microsoft servers as its infrastructure.

Romania is an eastern flank member of NATO and has faced physical and digital spillover of the confrontation between Russia and the West, particularly since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began. Airspace violations, drone shootdowns and even the strike of commercial vessels in its exclusive economic zone have been among the consequences.

The country  has also been targeted by cyber warfare. In May 2025, another known Russian APT actor attacked arms makers involved in supporting Ukraine, including those located in Romania; and just months after the war broke out, government websites were hit by a crude distributed denial-of-service attack, making Romanian public-authority and financial-sector websites unavailable for several hours.

Linus Höller is Defense News’ Europe correspondent and OSINT investigator. He reports on the arms deals, sanctions, and geopolitics shaping Europe and the world. He holds master’s degrees in WMD nonproliferation, terrorism studies, and international relations, and works in four languages: English, German, Russian, and Spanish.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth survives effort to impeach him | First Thing
articles.excerpt:
House Republicans block impeachment resolution that cited US military actions in Iran, Yemen and Venezuela. Plus, SS United States to be sunk to create artificial reef

Good morning. House Republicans...
articles.body_text:
House Republicans block impeachment resolution that cited US military actions in Iran, Yemen and Venezuela. Plus, SS United States to be sunk to create artificial reef

Good morning. House Republicans have blocked an effort to impeach Pete Hegseth. The defense secretary dismissed the impeachment resolution from a Republican lawmaker as “political spectacle”, saying it was an attempt to set up a “show trial”. Top Democrats announced their support for the resolution, but Republicans moved to kill it by referring it to the judiciary committee.

Thomas Massie’s 34-page resolution, which he read aloud on the House floor, centered on the Iran war. Hegseth said the articles targeted not just him but the troops who carried out his orders. He insisted that every operation the articles cite – including strikes on Iran and Yemen, attacks on alleged drug boats and the capture of Venezuela’s now former leader Nicolás Maduro – was lawful, ordered by Donald Trump and notified to Congress.

Why has the US Treasury chief reportedly moved? Scott Bessent has relocated from his home in the Washington area to a military base after an Iranian threat against his life, the New York Times reported. Bessent has led ‌the US sanctions and economic pressure campaign against Iran, called Operation Economic Outcast, since August.

Republicans have elected the longtime congressman Jim Jordan as their new leader in the House of Representatives, putting a strident defender of Donald Trump at the helm of their conference as they navigate the fallout from sweeping losses in last week’s midterm elections. Joseph Gedeon has this profile of the pugnacious Trump ideologue. We also have a gallery of newly elected Democrats, including Abdul El-Sayed and Annie Andrews, arriving in Washington for a new-member orientation day.

Democratic lawmakers in California are demanding answers from the Trump administration about the safety and whereabouts of an eight-year-old Haitian boy who they say was put in restraints and taken into custody by federal immigration officers at a check-in last week.

A spokesperson for the US Department of Homeland Security said Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) took the child into custody “out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child’s safety”.

An independent professor who reviewed the medical records of a prominent Gaza doctor held in an Israeli prison without charge for nearly 23 months has raised serious concerns about his health. Hussam Abu Safiya was detained at work in December 2024 and later held in solitary confinement at Rakefet, a notorious underground prison.

During a visit by a lawyer from Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) last summer, the doctor told of harsh conditions, untreated medical problems and severe food shortages.

One of Britain’s best-known entertainers and children’s authors, David Walliams, has been accused of using his celebrity status to prey on young women for sex. The allegations, which he denies, were revealed in a joint investigation by the Guardian and ITV News that spoke to 30 first-hand sources. A court rejected Walliams’s attempt to block publication after his legal team argued it was “highly likely” to lead him to attempt suicide. Michael Savage explains the main legal issues considered by the court – balancing Walliams’s right to privacy against the media’s right to publish. The full investigation is available here.

The estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has been jailed after US authorities said he cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units.

At least three people are dead and three critically injured after a car struck pedestrians on a Los Angeles street corner during rush hour. The driver, whose identity remains unknown, is in a critical condition in hospital.

The FDA has issued a new warning on GLP-1 weight-loss medications over a rare eye condition that could lead to sudden and permanent blindness.

Parents are suing to stop a Washington state trans sports ban that could require “invasive” genital exams.

An 11-month-old boy was found alive in South ⁠Carolina after he was believed to have been buried for ⁠about 24 hours, local police said.

A woman in Saudi Arabia has been sentenced to 100 lashes for giving birth outside marriage.

US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.

As Adrienne Matei explains, it takes about two weeks after vaccination for antibodies to develop in the body and provide protection, so the time is near to guard yourself before the holiday season. For those who are looking for some domestic advice, Victoria Turk has nailed how to solve 10 stubborn laundry problems – from stains to rough towels to “permastank”.

The SS United States is to finally be sunk off the coast of Florida to become an artificial reef. Internal fixtures and toxic materials have been removed, and divers will be able to visit the wreck at a depth of about 180ft as it becomes home to marine wildlife.

I found this read by Lana Crowe about the art of storyboarding – and why there is a pushback against AI being involved – fascinating. It features lots of great images in it, as does this photo gallery of Günther Kieser’s incredible psychedelic music posters for the likes of David Bowie, Jimi Hendrix and Diana Ross.

Developing countries have been left in limbo by the failure of some of the world’s biggest economies to flesh out their plans for new climate finance. Poor countries are supposed to receive $300bn a year from the governments of industrialized nations by 2035 to help them cope with the effects of extreme weather and shift to a low-carbon future. But many rich governments have not yet set out their targets.

You can follow the latest from Cop31 in Turkey with our live blog.

A new statue titled The Foot Soldier mocking Donald Trump has been installed on Washington’s National Mall, this time poking fun at bone spurs he was diagnosed with, which allowed him to defer the Vietnam war draft. Created by the Secret Handshake, a group of anonymous artists, the statue depicts the US president sitting down while rubbing his bare foot.

articles.title: Poultry and captive birds must be kept inside in England and Scotland because of bird flu
articles.excerpt:
Increased risk of devastating strain means restrictions imposed for second year in a row on those keeping birds

Poultry and captive birds across England and Scotland must be kept inside for the secon...
articles.body_text:
Increased risk of devastating strain means restrictions imposed for second year in a row on those keeping birds

Poultry and captive birds across England and Scotland must be kept inside for the second year in a row due to an increased risk of a devastating strain of bird flu.

The British government has issued an England-wide avian influenza prevention zone, meaning individuals with 50 or more poultry or captive birds must house them inside. A similar designation was made across the whole of Scotland on Tuesday.

Birdkeepers must also follow enhanced biosecurity measures including reporting changes in egg production and reporting suspected disease immediately to the Animal and Plant Health Agency.

The government said the declaration followed an increased risk and escalating number of confirmations of the highly pathogenic avian influenza, or bird flu, in kept and wild birds.

A prevention zone was also declared across all of England, Scotland and Wales in 2025.

Since 2014, the disease has been spreading rapidly and has devastated UK wild bird populations since the summer of 2021. It has also spread across an unusually broad range of species around the world, with four of the five main southern elephant seal populations reporting the disease. In some south Atlantic colonies, more than 90% of newborn pups have died, alongside about half of all adult females.

The disease has also been detected in humans, with 11 deaths recorded globally between 1 January and 4 August 2025.

This strain of bird flu causes illness and high death rates in birds, as well as flu-like symptoms and conjunctivitis in humans who come into close contact with infected animals.

The British government said the current risk to human health from bird flu remained very low.

The government says it does not anticipate an impact on the availability of Christmas turkeys or other seasonal poultry for consumers. The Food Safety Authority said properly cooked poultry and poultry products, including eggs, were safe to eat.

The UK chief veterinary officer, Christine Middlemiss, said: “Having avian influenza confirmed in your flock can be devastating. I understand the impact this disease can have on the poultry sector and am extremely grateful for the continued cooperation of the industry.”

articles.title: Burnham faces Badenoch at PMQs following huge windfarm approval – UK politics live
articles.excerpt:
PM to face leader of opposition before leaving for the Cop31 climate crisis summit

Good morning. Andy Burnham has got PMQs today, and after that he will leave for what looks like a rather hectic Turk...
articles.body_text:
PM to face leader of opposition before leaving for the Cop31 climate crisis summit

Good morning. Andy Burnham has got PMQs today, and after that he will leave for what looks like a rather hectic Turkey/Ireland trip which tomorrow will see him address the Cop31 climate summit in the morning, before attending his first major summit with EU leaders (and some other European leaders – it’s a European Political Community event) in Dublin later in the day.

Of the two events, the EPC is probably the more important for Burnham because it will give him the chance to clear the air ahead of the UK-EU summit next week, and because Burnham has made renegotiating the relationship with the EU a key aim of his premiership.

But Cop31 is important too because Burnham wants to show that he remains committed to the net zero climate agenda but that he is also “pragmatic” about pursuing this in a way that helps with cost of living pressures. This morning he has an announcement that will help in this respect; Downing Street has announced the next stage in two huge offshore wind projects.

One relates to the Vanguard East and Vanguard West projects. No 10 says:

double quotation markEnergy company RWE, together with global investment firm KKR, have announced a total investment of £12bn, believed to be the biggest of its kind in UK history to date. It will give the green light to its Vanguard West and Vanguard East offshore wind farms, set to be operational by 2030 and delivering clean, secure, homegrown power to homes and businesses that will protect families from global fossil fuel price shocks …

On top of bolstering the UK’s green energy future, the investment will support more than 2,400 jobs during construction and operation, and once operational, the wind farms will have the capacity to supply the equivalent of around three million UK homes …

The decision marks a major milestone for the project, with the developers now making their final investment commitment to deliver the projects. Onshore works are already well advanced, with construction offshore set to begin in early 2027.

The other relates to Berwick Bank B. No 10 says:

double quotation markOn top of this, Scottish-headquartered SSE has announced that the latest phase of its major offshore wind farm, Berwick Bank B, will back 2,677 skilled jobs in manufacturing, engineering and project delivery across the north of England and Scotland, with the company contracting Siemens Energy for the manufacturing of wind turbines and substation platforms. This includes the creation of 130 new project delivery roles in Glasgow and Montrose.

At its full capacity, Berwick Bank, off the east coast of Scotland, could become the world’s largest offshore wind farm, capable of meeting more than 6% of current UK electricity demand.

Welcoming these announcements, Burnham said:

double quotation markThis major investment in UK renewables is a vote of confidence for building in Britain. And it is great news for billpayers because every turbine we put up is power under British control, not at the mercy of events on the other side of the world.

Ajit Niranjan has a separate live blog covering Cop31.

10am: Angela Rayner, the housing secretary, gives evidence to the Commons housing committee.

10.50am: Lucy Powell, the education secretary, gives a speech to the Association of Colleges annual conference in Birmingham.

11am: Louise Casey gives a speech at the National Children and Adult Services conference in Liverpool.

Noon: Andy Burnham faces Kemi Badenoch at PMQs.

Noon: Morgan McSweeney, Keir Starmer’s former chief of staff, gives evidence to the Lords constitution committee about constitutional safeguards.

1pm: Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, gives a speech to the annual airlines’ conference in London.

2.15pm: John Healey, the chancellor, gives evidence to the Commons Treasury committee about the budget.

Afternoon: Burnham leaves London to fly to the Cop31 climate conference in Turkey.

I’m afraid we are no longer able to have comments open below the line every day on this blog. If you want to contact me, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this email to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints.

Badenoch says the government is legislating to ban drilling off Scotland. That is ludicrous, she says.

Burnham says the Jackdaw gas field has been approved. And the new windfarms are going ahead. He goes on:

double quotation markIf she wants to,address energy policy in this house, perhaps we can talk about why energy bills went up and up under the party opposite. Perhaps we can discuss how they lost public control and lost control of people’s bills and left people paying more and more.

Badenoch says Rosebank has not been approved because Ed Miliband was not in favour when he was energy secretary,

double quotation markHe called Rosebank climate vandalism. But then he also thought cosying up to Russell Brand would make him prime minister. So I don’t think we need to trust his judgement.

Burnham says Rosebank would have been approved if it had not been for the last goverment messing up the licensing process. He says it is a quasi-judicial matter now. But he highlights the windfarm projects announced today. (See 8.55am.)

Badenoch jokes about Andy Burnham being in the audience for a speech by the cabinet secretary, Antonia Romeo, last night.

double quotation markHe’s supposed to be telling her his plan, not sat in the audience while she tells him hers.

She asks why the plan for the Rosebank oil field was in the budget calculations when it has not been approved.

Burnham says Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision.

Referring to the Tory plans for welfare cuts announced yesterday, he says:

double quotation markDoes she accept that so many of the people affected by what she announced are working people, people whose incomes will be hit hard in a cost of living crisis? I think the honourable lady needs to answer as to why she is making the cost of living crisis harder for people by the cuts she’s just announced.

Badenoch references a Guardian story about Labour MPs being concerned about the lack of ambition in the 10-year plan and she jokes about reports that it will include merging the DVLA with the DVSA. “Exciting stuff,” she says.

Burnham picks up on Badenoch mentioning the budget, and he says it was the most popular budget for years. On issues like social care and Neets, the government is taking big decisions, he says.

Kemi Badenoch asks if it is true that Andy Burnham is so short of ideas for his 10-year plan for Britain that he has asked the Boston Consulting Group to help.

Burnham says he will present his 10-year plans to MPs before the Christmas recess.

(Last week he said it might not come until January.)

Claire Hanna, the SDLP leader, says MPs would not let one party at Westminster to stop the Commons operating. But that is what is happening at Stormont, she says, because of the conduct of the DUP. Stormont is in its “dying days” without reform, she says.

Burnham says all MPs want to see Stormont up and running and delivering. He says the Northern Ireland is working with the parties to agree a budget, and he is considering further options for reform.

Andy Burnham starts by saying all MP remember the sacrifice of all those who have served their country.

No veterans should have to sleep on the streets, he says. He says he has written to councils asking him to help him end rough sleeping for veterans.

Here is the list of MPs who have got a question.

Back to Labour’s EU policy, and Stuart Ingham, head of the policy unit in No 10 when Keir Starmer was PM, has written a long and subtle article in the New Statesman arguing that, rather than focus on trying to rejoin the EU fully, or just the single market, Andy Burnham would be better off focusing for now on goals around which Labour could unite.

double quotation markWhere does Rejoin fit into this? If there was a referendum tomorrow, I’d vote to undo a mistake. Perhaps for some, saying so is the first necessary step of a longer journey. But I fear divisions about questions we don’t have to answer at the moment will be a barrier to unity over the questions that we do. The soft Euroscepticism inherent in Labour may harden at just the wrong moment …

Then there are the voters. The Prime Minister speaks with them when he says that Brexit has been a failure and the status quo isn’t good enough. There is scope to sell an economic and security partnership, and leave Reform and the Tories to fight over a tiny pool of voters that think it’s been a success. The arguments against Rejoin are stronger: they allow the populist right to avoid defending the Brexit it has delivered and go straight to its home territory – emotional arguments about democracy, betrayal and elites.

The reset should be promoted on its own terms. It can be a stepping stone for those with a destination in mind and a leap forward to a better deal for those that don’t. Labour, for now, is a party with Rejoiners in it rather than a Rejoiner party.

When Ingham was in Downing Street, he was working on the deals on food exports, energy policy and youth mobility that are due to be presented as a reset moment at the UK-EU summit next week. The EU regularly says it will not allow cherry picking, and that to gain the all the advantages of the single market, states have to accept all the obligations (including free movement). Ingham points out that, in practice, it is not that straightword, which is why there are opportunities for Britain that don’t involve full membership or full single market membership. He explains:

double quotation markThe government I advised on Europe policy made headway in getting the UK included in both the Made in Europe and European defence programmes. The EU has agreed that Britain can participate in the Ukraine loan scheme – so Kyiv can buy weapons and munitions from British firms with European capital. The UK is within the scope of draft clauses of the Industrial Accelerator Act, meaning its companies may be able to bid for large procurement contracts. The emissions trading agreement, expected to be signed this month, paves the way for British manufacturers to be exempt from Europe’s carbon import taxes, without which reindustrialisation cannot happen. Although the EU will not want it presented this way, that emissions agreement is Britain being allowed access and rights within the parts of the single market where it follows the rules. The food and drink and electricity deals, pitched to the EU as about food security and energy security, are the same. Cherries can be picked when it’s in everyone’s common security interest.

In a Bluesky thread on the Joe Martin story (see 11.04am), Will Hayward, the Welsh political commentator, says he thinks Martin may soon defect from Reform UK to Restore Britain. “Mr Martin has been making kissy faces at Restore for a while,” Hayward says. “Reform sources within that group tell me the party are deeply concerned at Restore eating into their vote and potential defections.”

Hayward points out that Rupert Lowe, the Restore Britain MP and party leader, has been tweeting in support of Martin. In one message, Lowe said:

double quotation markIf the Welsh Parliament is going to shut down legitimate debate around demographic security and immigration, the Restore Britain answer is quite straightforward...

Roll back devolution and shut down the Welsh parliament.

The leader of Reform in Wales has said her party stands with a member who was banned from speaking in the Welsh parliament after claiming white British people were being replaced in the UK, the Press Association reports.

Reform’s Joe Martin was handed the ban yesterday after his comments were described as “discriminatory” and “offensive” by the Llywydd (presiding officer), Huw Irranca-Davies.

Helen Jenner, the Reform UK leader in the Senedd, posted a message on social media this morning saying:

double quotation markReform stands with Joe Martin.

Freedom of speech must be protected at all costs.

Speaking in the Senedd yesterday, Martin, the MS for Caerdydd Penarth, said:

double quotation markCan I have a statement from your government on the demographic replacement of white British people taking place in the UK? Because the scale of change has been breathtaking. Mass immigration and differing birth rates mean that, in just 37 years’ time, in 2063, we will be a minority in our own country. That change has already taken place in London, Birmingham, Leicester, Slough, Luton and Manchester, and I don’t want it to happen here.

Indeed, at every opportunity, the majority of the electorate have wanted less immigration so that their nation can be preserved. A nation is not an economic zone, it’s not a hotel, and neither is it a charity. It’s a family, which is capable of absorbing people of all races if done at a sensible rate, but not if it’s replaced altogether.

Welsh minister Heledd Fychan responded by asking for a ruling on whether the comments were in line with Senedd rules, adding:

double quotation markWe have a duty for every single member of our communities that we represent. I reject division and hate. We had a question earlier to the prif weinidog (first minister) around antisemitism. We cannot differentiate between people of different religions, different sexuality, different skin colour. We are a government for everyone here in Wales, we are supposed to be a Senedd for everyone here in Wales. I reject wholeheartedly the division that is spouted by those members.

Later in the afternoon, Irranca-Davies said he considered the comments made by Martin to be “unnecessarily provocative and deliberately offensive”. He said:

double quotation markWhilst it is always possible to raise legitimate policy matters in relation to immigration in this siambr [chamber], the focus of that contribution on race and ethnicity was clearly discriminatory, offensive, and detracted from the dignity of the Senedd.

This is not the first time the member has pushed the boundaries in his contributions, and I have previously warned him about his conduct.

Until I receive a clear indication that the member understands the boundaries of acceptable parliamentary conduct and apologises to the siambr, we will not be calling the member to speak.

Reform is the largest opposition group to the Plaid Cymru-led government.

articles.title: Slain New Jersey mom’s bedroom furniture removed by investigators months after unsolved stabbing
articles.excerpt:
A former FBI agent and private investigator Robert Strang analyzes law enforcement's return to the property after five months of investigation into Hanlon's death.

CHESTER, N.J. – A neighbor confirme...
articles.body_text:
A former FBI agent and private investigator Robert Strang analyzes law enforcement's return to the property after five months of investigation into Hanlon's death.

CHESTER, N.J. – A neighbor confirmed investigators removed what appeared to be a headboard, hamper and possible comforter or quilt from the property where Brooke Hanlon, 35, was found stabbed to death earlier this year.

Fox News Digital was on the scene outside the home on Pottersville Road in Chester, New Jersey last week and witnessed investigators carrying scads of those items wrapped in brown paper and marked with evidence tape out of the Hanlon home.

Hanlon, a psychotherapist and mother, was found fatally stabbed in the home on June 6. Her husband, James "Conor" Hanlon, had called 911 from the home after his wife was found stabbed there. No arrests have been made.

He was seen speaking with police on Wednesday afternoon, his neighbors said.

Law enforcement personnel remove evidence from the home of Conor Hanlon in Chester, N.J., Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Hanlon's wife, Brooke Hanlon, was found dead in their home in June. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)

COPS RETURN TO NEW JERSEY MOTHER'S HOME MONTHS AFTER SHE WAS FOUND STABBED AND HUSBAND CALLED 911

On Thursday, Fox News Digital witnessed officers remove what appeared to be a large comforter from a second-story window at the house.
