articles.title: Trump administration again boycotts UN human rights review
articles.excerpt: The United States ⁠⁠has again boycotted a United Nations examination of its human rights record, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations under President Donald Trump are surging to lev...
articles.body_text:
The United States ⁠⁠has again boycotted a United Nations examination of its human rights record, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations under President Donald Trump are surging to levels not seen in decades.

US representatives on Tuesday failed to show up at the UN in Geneva for the review, which all 193 UN member states undergo every four to five years.

“The delegation of the United States is not present in the room,” UN Human Rights Council President Sidharto Reza Suryodipuro, of Indonesia, announced as the session was set to begin.

The US refusal to participate prompted the UN body to delay examining the US human rights record until January. This is the second year in a row that Washington has skipped its own review.

The US withdrew from the council in February 2025 shortly after Trump began his second presidential term, claiming it was biased against Israel.

The Trump administration has been a fierce critic of the UN, withdrawing Washington from key agencies, slashing its funding and bypassing the body in launching the war on Iran.

A US State Department spokesperson said participation would imply endorsement of the council’s work.

“[We] give no credibility to the agency,” the spokesperson said.

“This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own ‘values’ as it pushes anti-American rhetoric,” the official added, without responding to allegations about the US record.

The 47-member council has not directly criticised Washington’s rights record. However, experts have expressed alarm over issues such as migrant deportations, which Washington maintains are carried out in accordance with US immigration law.

UN documents show countries had planned to raise issues such as abortion access and the death penalty.

US and international non-governmental organisations also sent nearly 200 UN submissions covering ⁠⁠topics from migration to racial discrimination.

“Enough is enough,” Jamil Dakwar, of the American Civil Liberties Union, told ⁠⁠reporters in Geneva.

“We’ve seen attacks on fundamental human rights and civil liberties unprecedented in generations,” he added.

Fourteen countries are due to take part in ⁠⁠the review process in Geneva this month. During Trump’s first term in office, the US submitted its UN Universal Periodic Review (UPR) report.

Eric Tistounet, a visiting professor at the Geneva Graduate Institute who was the council’s first secretary, said the US walkout could affect the credibility of the council’s review system.

“If the predominant global power, which has always claimed to adhere to the human rights norms, doesn’t show up and doesn’t even justify why, then you are in big trouble,” he said.

articles.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Lindsay Clancy judge denies double jeopardy motion and explains jury notes after deadlock
articles.excerpt: Attorney Randolph Rice says prosecutors can use lessons from the first trial to refine their case. He also explains why he believes Judge William Sullivan’s order rejected Clancy’s double-jeopardy arg...
articles.body_text:
Attorney Randolph Rice says prosecutors can use lessons from the first trial to refine their case. He also explains why he believes Judge William Sullivan’s order rejected Clancy’s double-jeopardy argument.

The Massachusetts judge overseeing the murder case against Lindsay Clancy has denied her motion to dismiss the case on double jeopardy claims, clearing the way for a retrial in the strangling deaths of her three young children that some experts believe could have a better chance at a guilty verdict.

"Because the Court concludes that there was a manifest necessity for a mistrial based on the jury’s deadlock, a retrial on the murder indictments does not violate Clancy’s right not to be placed in double jeopardy," Judge William Sullivan wrote in a 17-page order and memorandum made public Monday.

Clancy's 26-day trial ended with a deadlocked jury on Sept. 4, with jurors later saying publicly that 11 of them accepted her insanity defense and one wanted to find her guilty of first-degree murder for what the holdout called the "methodical" slayings of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

LINDSAY CLANCY DEFENSE FILES MOTION TO DISMISS UNDER DOUBLE JEOPARDY GROUNDS, WITH FOCUS ON HOLDOUT JUROR

Judge William Sullivan indicates he was going to declare a mistrial before changing course and giving Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney one hour to appeal, as the jury in the case has indicated that they are unable to reach a verdict on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Had the motion been granted, Clancy would not face a potential second trial, said Randolph Rice, a trial attorney and former prosecutor who is not connected to the case.

Now, he says, the order gives prosecutors a chance to address what went wrong with their case in the first trial.

"I think there's real possibility that DA [Tim] Cruz says, 'We're going back to trial ... and we have learned from our mistakes,'" Rice said.

Among the lessons learned, Rice said, may be that Plymouth County prosecutors did not show jurors enough empathy when presenting their case after 11 of the 12 jurors voted against them.

What a second trial may look like remains unclear as prosecutors have so far declined to publicly commit to bringing the same or different charges.

Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Pool Photo by Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)

Deliberations began on Aug. 27. On Sept. 1, they sent the first of several notes explaining their deadlocked situation.

"After many hours of deliberation, we are unable to come to a unanimous verdict," that first note said, according to Sullivan, who instructed them to keep trying.

They sent a similar note on Sept. 2, and Sullivan, without objection from lawyers on either side, read them what's known as a Tuey-Rodriguez charge — an instruction given to hung jurors encouraging them to reexamine their views with an open mind while reminding jurors they should not abandon honestly held beliefs to reach their verdict.

On Sept. 3, Sullivan received another note reading, "A member of the jury is unable to follow the instructions regarding reasonable doubt. How should we proceed?"

ATTORNEY FOR LONE HOLDOUT JUROR IN LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL PUSHES BACK ON CLAIMS OF REFUSING THE LAW

Michael P. Desronvil, the juror whose refusal to join the other 11 led to a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial. (Fugitive TV)

In his order, Sullivan wrote that he was skeptical of the allegation that the holdout was "genuinely" unable to follow instructions regarding reasonable doubt and decided to hold a "limited inquiry" into each juror's ability to follow the law.

Prosecutors had opposed voir dire, and the defense asked for the holdout to be replaced with an alternate. The defense then asked for the judge to ask the foreperson to expand on what she meant in her latest note, and prosecutors objected, arguing that a question like that would improperly intrude into the deliberation process. Sullivan agreed with the commonwealth and asked each juror, "Are you able to follow my instructions on the law that were given to you earlier in the trial?"

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR WON'T HAVE TO TURN OVER PHONE OR FACE INQUIRY, JUDGE SAYS

District Attorney Timothy Cruz leaves Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, September, 3, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

Each juror answered "affirmatively and credibly," Sullivan wrote.

Prosecutors and the defense agreed that the court should also reinstruct the jury, as a whole, about reasonable doubt, and Sullivan did so. Afterward, however, Clancy's defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, again asked for the holdout to be replaced with an alternate, and Sullivan denied his motion.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S PUSH TO PROBE HOLDOUT JUROR HITS SNAG BEFORE PIVOTAL RETRIAL HEARING

Later on Sept. 3, the foreperson sent another note, directly accusing the holdout of ignoring reasonable doubts about the case, according to Sullivan.

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM

Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"[Juror Doe] has made statements acknowledging doubt but refuses to apply it to the verdict as the law states," she wrote. "This is why we cannot come to a unanimous decision."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Jurors were sent home for the day. Before deliberations resumed on Sept. 4, Sullivan and counsel on both sides discussed the latest note. Sullivan gave jurors another instruction on reasonable doubt and following the law and told them that future notes should not identify anyone's vote based on their juror number. Two hours later, with no movement in the deliberation room, Sullivan said he planned to declare a mistrial, over Reddington's objection.

He granted a one-hour stay as the defense appealed to the state's Supreme Judicial Court. A single justice summarily denied the defense’s emergency request, then Sullivan declared a mistrial.

LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT

Clancy's defense later filed a motion to dismiss on double jeopardy grounds, arguing that there was no "manifest necessity" for the court to declare a mistrial and that as a result, a new trial would violate Clancy's Fifth Amendment rights.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"Clancy contends that there was no manifest necessity for a mistrial because the Court failed to consider the alternative of inquiring into the meaning of the foreperson's notes and questioning Juror Doe to determine whether there was good cause to discharge Juror Doe," Sullivan wrote.

Juror Doe is Michael Desronvil, who came forward publicly in an interview with Fox News and said that he never had doubts about his view on Clancy's guilt.

Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Pool Photo by Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)

Deliberations began on Aug. 27. On Sept. 1, they sent the first of several notes explaining their deadlocked situation.

"After many hours of deliberation, we are unable to come to a unanimous verdict," that first note said, according to Sullivan, who instructed them to keep trying.

They sent a similar note on Sept. 2, and Sullivan, without objection from lawyers on either side, read them what's known as a Tuey-Rodriguez charge — an instruction given to hung jurors encouraging them to reexamine their views with an open mind while reminding jurors they should not abandon honestly held beliefs to reach their verdict.

On Sept. 3, Sullivan received another note reading, "A member of the jury is unable to follow the instructions regarding reasonable doubt. How should we proceed?"

ATTORNEY FOR LONE HOLDOUT JUROR IN LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL PUSHES BACK ON CLAIMS OF REFUSING THE LAW

Michael P. Desronvil, the juror whose refusal to join the other 11 led to a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial. (Fugitive TV)

In his order, Sullivan wrote that he was skeptical of the allegation that the holdout was "genuinely" unable to follow instructions regarding reasonable doubt and decided to hold a "limited inquiry" into each juror's ability to follow the law.

Prosecutors had opposed voir dire, and the defense asked for the holdout to be replaced with an alternate. The defense then asked for the judge to ask the foreperson to expand on what she meant in her latest note, and prosecutors objected, arguing that a question like that would improperly intrude into the deliberation process. Sullivan agreed with the commonwealth and asked each juror, "Are you able to follow my instructions on the law that were given to you earlier in the trial?"

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR WON'T HAVE TO TURN OVER PHONE OR FACE INQUIRY, JUDGE SAYS

District Attorney Timothy Cruz leaves Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, September, 3, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

Each juror answered "affirmatively and credibly," Sullivan wrote.

Prosecutors and the defense agreed that the court should also reinstruct the jury, as a whole, about reasonable doubt, and Sullivan did so. Afterward, however, Clancy's defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, again asked for the holdout to be replaced with an alternate, and Sullivan denied his motion.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S PUSH TO PROBE HOLDOUT JUROR HITS SNAG BEFORE PIVOTAL RETRIAL HEARING

Later on Sept. 3, the foreperson sent another note, directly accusing the holdout of ignoring reasonable doubts about the case, according to Sullivan.

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM

Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"[Juror Doe] has made statements acknowledging doubt but refuses to apply it to the verdict as the law states," she wrote. "This is why we cannot come to a unanimous decision."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Jurors were sent home for the day. Before deliberations resumed on Sept. 4, Sullivan and counsel on both sides discussed the latest note. Sullivan gave jurors another instruction on reasonable doubt and following the law and told them that future notes should not identify anyone's vote based on their juror number. Two hours later, with no movement in the deliberation room, Sullivan said he planned to declare a mistrial, over Reddington's objection.

He granted a one-hour stay as the defense appealed to the state's Supreme Judicial Court. A single justice summarily denied the defense’s emergency request, then Sullivan declared a mistrial.

LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT

Clancy's defense later filed a motion to dismiss on double jeopardy grounds, arguing that there was no "manifest necessity" for the court to declare a mistrial and that as a result, a new trial would violate Clancy's Fifth Amendment rights.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"Clancy contends that there was no manifest necessity for a mistrial because the Court failed to consider the alternative of inquiring into the meaning of the foreperson's notes and questioning Juror Doe to determine whether there was good cause to discharge Juror Doe," Sullivan wrote.

Juror Doe is Michael Desronvil, who came forward publicly in an interview with Fox News and said that he never had doubts about his view on Clancy's guilt.

articles.title: First-ever Collaborative Combat Aircraft fly in formation, demonstrate air combat maneuvers
articles.excerpt:
For the first time, the U.S. Air Force’s semi-autonomous drones flew in formation and executed air combat maneuvers.

Shield’s Hivemind, the autonomy software that “runs” Collaborative Combat Aircraft...
articles.body_text:
For the first time, the U.S. Air Force’s semi-autonomous drones flew in formation and executed air combat maneuvers.

Shield’s Hivemind, the autonomy software that “runs” Collaborative Combat Aircraft flights, helped multiple CCAs fly in a “multi-ship” formation and execute beyond-visual-range counter-air tactics, according to a recent company release.

The release did not specify how many aircraft flew in formation or which CCA participated in the Oct. 26 exercise.

“We are excited that the aircraft and mission systems are reaching a level of integration to start showing what Hivemind can really do,” Todd Wesley, vice president of Hivemind engineering at Shield, said in the announcement.

Each flight generates data that contributes to a software release, per the statement, which supports decisions on testing and fielding.

“The combined Hivemind and aircraft software release process is nearing the point where the Air Force can fly a sortie, update the software overnight and fly again the next day,” Wesley said. “I’m grateful to the Air Force operators, engineers and test teams who fly with us and help us build trust on every flight.”

The demonstration comes as the Air Force announced its intention to have 500 combat-ready, semi-autonomous systems by 2032, with an overall fleet size of 1,000. For the CCA program, the service’s fiscal 2027 budget request included $996.5 million in procurement funding, as well as $150 million in advanced procurement for the following fiscal year and $1.37 billion in continued research and development, for a total program request of $2.37 billion.

The new Shield milestone in the CCA program comes after a F-22 raptor completed airborne tactical command and in-flight control of a YFQ-44A last month, serving as a “quarterback” and giving high-level directives to the Anduril-made CCA.

Meanwhile, Shield AI announced last week its decision to acquire Echodyne in a $5.3 billion transaction to expand the contractor’s drone-warfare capabilities.

The move to absorb Echodyne — which can produce next-generation, solid-state radar systems — was said to support Shield’s expansion into different areas of unmanned systems.

Cristina Stassis is a reporter covering stories surrounding the defense industry, national security, military/veteran affairs and more. She previously worked as an editorial fellow for Defense News in 2024 where she assisted the newsroom in breaking news across Sightline Media Group.

articles.title: Judge who sentenced Russell Brand praised for dispelling rape myths
articles.excerpt:
Criminal Bar Association and campaigners hail Mr Justice Bennathan for delivering remarks with ‘piercing clarity’

The judge who sentenced Russell Brand has been praised for dispelling rape myths with...
articles.body_text:
Criminal Bar Association and campaigners hail Mr Justice Bennathan for delivering remarks with ‘piercing clarity’

The judge who sentenced Russell Brand has been praised for dispelling rape myths with “piercing clarity”.

Mr Justice Bennathan’s sentencing remarks were particularly welcomed given that rape myths had played a part in the trial. He was also lauded for calling out “enablers” who witnessed sexual assaults by the comedian.

Sentencing Brand to 10 and a half years on Monday for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others, Bennathan said: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent.”

Andrew Thomas KC, the chair of the Criminal Bar Association, and Kama Melly KC, its vice-chair, said: “We welcome the piercing clarity of the judge’s statement. Myths about rape and sexual assault must play no part in our culture or in our courtrooms. Raping or sexually assaulting someone is a crime, and blame lies entirely with the perpetrator.

“Victims of sexual violence should know that when they go to the prosecution authorities, their evidence will be judged fairly and properly. As the verdicts in Russell Brand’s case show, a properly directed jury will not be put off by a defendant’s appeal to rape myths.”

Ciara Bergman, the chief executive of Rape Crisis England & Wales, said Bennathan’s remarks were “hugely important” at the end of such a high-profile trial. “We’re pleased he emphasised and upheld women’s rights and freedoms, and recognised the profound courage of the women who came forward, and what they endured during the trial, too,” she said.

“This recognition stands in stark contrast to the appalling accusations made by Brand’s defence barrister, who perpetuated myths, misconceptions and conceptions about rape, such as needing to have fought, screamed or reported immediately for it to be considered a credible allegation. Of course this is not the case; there are a range of ways in which people respond to the threat of an imminent sexual assault and all of them are valid.”

Deniz Uğur, the deputy director of the End Violence Against Women Coalition, said rape myths should be prohibited. “The judge’s comments are welcome given the significant role that rape myths played in this trial, which in turn have influenced public discussions about the case,” she said. “This will be having a profound effect not only on the women involved in this case, but on survivors exposed to victim-blaming and misconceptions online and in their daily lives.”

On Tuesday, Labour’s deputy leader, Lucy Powell, praised Bennathan’s “incredibly powerful” sentencing remarks, contrasting them with the “depressing” nature of the cross-examination of Brand’s victims by his barrister, Ian Winter KC.

The judge also took aim at Brand’s “enablers” who witnessed Brand sexually assault women in front of them at a radio station and TV studio. He said of the former incident: “No doubt your companions thought it was outrageous laddish behaviour that only you could get away with. It was outrageous and possibly laddish, but also a criminal sexual offence, and as it turns out you haven’t got away with it.”

Bennathan told Brand the assault at the TV studio showed “your staggering arrogance, and it shows how your entourage indulged your dreadful behaviour”.

Bergman described the comments as “crucial”, adding: “This case and the national response to it is about more than just one man, it is about everyone who laughed along, didn’t speak up and/or looked away, even when it was happening right in front of them. They may not have committed Brand’s crimes, but they contributed to the culture that meant he went on harming other women with impunity for so long.”

Uğur similarly welcomed Bennathan’s remarks, saying it was “critically important to look at the many institutions and individuals that enabled [Brand’s] behaviour”.

Information and support for anyone affected by rape or sexual abuse issues is available from the following organisations. In the UK, Rape Crisis offers support on 0808 500 2222 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland, or 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland. In the US, Rainn offers support on 800-656-4673. In Australia, support is available at 1800Respect (1800 737 732). Other international helplines can be found at ibiblio.org/rcip/internl.html

articles.title: Woman jailed for posing as man to dupe partner into sex found guilty of similar deception
articles.excerpt:
Jury finds Blade Silvano, who presented herself as a male army veteran, guilty of six counts of sexual assault

A woman serving a prison sentence for sexual assault after pretending to be a man and du...
articles.body_text:
Jury finds Blade Silvano, who presented herself as a male army veteran, guilty of six counts of sexual assault

A woman serving a prison sentence for sexual assault after pretending to be a man and duping a woman into a physical relationship has been found guilty of tricking another woman into a similar abusive partnership.

In both cases, Blade Silvano, 44, met the women on an online dating site and falsely claimed she was a man who had served in the armed forces before meeting them in person and sexually assaulting them.

Both women said Silvano tricked them into believing she was male and neither had any idea they were being deceived.

Silvano was jailed in 2023 in Cambridge after a jury heard she carried out the deception using a blindfold, sex toy and a “wholly fake persona”. Silvano and her victim even became engaged as a man and woman.

On Tuesday, a jury at Caernarfon crown court in north Wales found her guilty of six counts of sexual assault by penetration between November 2022 and the following June after being told she had carried out the same sort of deception on another woman.

Using the alias “Hunter”, Silvano began messaging the victim on the Plenty of Fish site before meeting her for sex, always keeping the lights very low and not allowing herself to be touched intimately.

Silvano claimed to be a captain and surgeon in the army and on one occasion claimed “his” condom had broken as they had sex. Silvano assured the alleged victim it was “very unlikely” she would get pregnant and told her: “Trust me, I’m a doctor.”

The jury was told the woman noticed her partner sounded a “little feminine” and began to have doubts about their “odd” sex life.

Eventually, the victim received a call from Silvano’s long-term partner, a woman, who said the person she’d known as “Hunter” was female, the court heard.

The victim told police she felt sick when she learned of the deception, saying: “I thought it was some sort of joke.” In court, she said: “I believed I was in a relationship with a straight, heterosexual man. I would never go out with a woman.”

Philip Clemo, prosecuting, told the jury Silvano was a gifted con artist and suggested she was inspired by the myth of Zeus turning into a bull.

The Cambridgeshire offences took place in 2016 and 2017. Using the fake name Blade Mendez, Silvano presented herself as a male army veteran throughout a two-year relationship.

She would send the victim photos of herself apparently shaving her face and would pretend to urinate standing up.

Silvano, of Shropshire, would not allow the victim to touch her genitals, claiming to be “body conscious due to injuries sustained in the army”. Silvano and the woman got engaged and she was encouraged to try on wedding dresses and book a registrar.

The victim accidentally uncovered Silvano’s deception after coming across her on Facebook in September 2018 “in a completely different living situation”. Silvano was found guilty of two counts of assault by penetration.

Silvano will be sentenced for the six sexual assaults next month. Judge Jones ordered a pre-sentence report so that the risk she posed could be assessed.

articles.title: Liberal podcasters tell TPUSA to ‘f--- off’ as Charlie Kirk backlash costs them advertisers
articles.excerpt: Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan, co-hosts of the 'I've Had It' podcast, address the backlash after apologizing for laughing at a joke about digging up Kirk’s body. (Credit: I've Had it Podcast - Nov...
articles.body_text:
Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan, co-hosts of the 'I've Had It' podcast, address the backlash after apologizing for laughing at a joke about digging up Kirk’s body. (Credit: I've Had it Podcast - Nov. 8)

A source in the office of a prominent nationally elected Democrat called "I've Had It" podcast host Jennifer Welch a "sicko" after she allegedly sought help managing backlash over a joke about digging up Charlie Kirk 's body. Welch denied the source's account as she and co-host Angie Sullivan renewed their attacks on Turning Point USA , with Sullivan telling the conservative organization to "f— all the way off" despite the hosts' earlier apology.

The controversy has also cost the podcast advertisers. Cash App announced it was ending its sponsorship, saying on social media: "We do not condone violence of any kind, and we are no longer sponsors of this podcast." Luxury bedding company Boll & Branch also reportedly dropped its sponsorship, while Turning Point USA's Andrew Kolvet claimed on X that several other advertisers had withdrawn their support.

The hosts apologized over the weekend, but Sullivan subsequently told TPUSA to "f--- off" while Welch said her apology was motivated by her own convictions rather than pressure from the conservative organization.

"Alright there's a huge online, cancellation campaign from all the titty babies over at Turning Point who want the 'I've Had It' podcast cancelled," Welch said in a video posted to the podcast's YouTube channel. She accused Turning Point USA of "spearheading" the campaign because they're "losers and they lost" and "want to prove to their donors we can cancel libs."

SOCIAL MEDIA HORRIFIED BY DAVE CHAPPELLE’S SICK ‘JOKE’ ABOUT CHARLIE KIRK’S MURDER

Co-hosts of the "I’ve Had It" podcast, Jennifer Welch and Angie "Pumps" Sullivan spoke on their show. ("I've Had It" YouTube channel)

"When we apologize for laughing at a joke on our podcast, that wasn't for you. That was for us," Welch continued. "Because someone I loved very much died from gun violence two years ago and I just didn't feel good about that. And that apology was so that when I advocate for common sense gun reform that I'm doing it clean and clear. I don't expect you to understand this because at Turning Point y'all laugh at violence all the time."

FAR-LEFT PODCASTER CALLS FOR 'PISTOLS FIRING' TOWARD JD VANCE, DEFEATING HIM IN 2028

A Democratic source told Fox News Digital that Welch called them while seeking advice on how to manage the fallout from her comments. According to the source, Welch blamed Turning Point USA for the controversy rather than expressing remorse.

"I am not Turning Point. I'm a national Dem and we don't need people like her in this party because it is exactly what we don’t like about the hard right," the source said. The source also called Welch a "sicko" and estimated that the podcast had lost "tens of thousands" of dollars in sponsorships over the weekend. The source further alleged that Welch's team used ChatGPT to help formulate a response to the controversy and identify "ways out of this."

A supporter attends a vigil in memory of right-wing activist Charlie Kirk who was fatally shot during an event at Utah Valley University, outside the headquarters of Turning Point USA in Phoenix, Ariz., Sept.19, 2025.

Welch denied the claims in a text message to Fox News Digital, saying she had not spoken with a top Democrat and that the podcast had not used ChatGPT. "Those are both wholly untrue," she said.

A YEAR AFTER CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER, SOME COMICS ARE CALLING OUT JOKES ABOUT HIS DEATH

"We laughed at an insensitive joke. We regret it, and we apologized," Welch said. She added that the podcast had removed the segment and donated to Everytown for Gun Safety, a gun-control advocacy organization.

"Turning Point, the group leading the cancellation against us, mocks violence and never apologizes," Welch added. "We still have plenty of advertisers and we aren’t going anywhere."

Jennifer Welch, co-host of the "I've Had It" podcast was an Oklahoma City-based interior designer who starred in the short-lived Bravo reality show "Sweet Home Oklahoma" from 2017-2018. ("I've Had It" YouTube channel)

While discussing their apology, Welch called TPUSA a "hateful organization," and Sullivan said she was "not going to be lectured by these people."

"These people support Representatives to Congress that protect pedophiles and sex traffickers. They're completely fine with American citizens being gunned down on the streets of Minnesota. They're fine with putting people in cages and treating them like animals," she continued. "And for those of you at Turning Point who are worried that I don't talk enough, but yet, you don't believe in universal human rights, I want you to hear me: F— off. F— all the way off."

TURNING POINT USA TURNS THE TABLES ON 'SATURDAY NIGHT LIVE' AFTER LATE-NIGHT SKETCH MOCKS CAMPUS RECRUITERS

The controversy began during an episode last week in which Welch and Sullivan read social media posts celebrating Democratic victories in the midterm elections. Both laughed after Welch read one post saying, "We’re digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again." The hosts also suggested, without presenting evidence, that Kirk's accused killer supported President Donald Trump. Voter records, however, showed that he was unaffiliated and had not voted in the previous two general elections.

After the episode sparked backlash, Welch and Sullivan posted an apology Saturday saying they had laughed at an "insensitive joke" and "should not have laughed." They said there was "nothing funny about gun violence."

The hosts' remarks also drew criticism from Democrats, including strategist Kaivan Shroff. "They are not helping Democrats," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "They are hijacking the attention Democrats actually earned at the ballot box."

Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

articles.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.excerpt:
The victory comes after an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones

A UK court has overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago.

London's Judicial Committee of the ...
articles.body_text:
The victory comes after an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones

A UK court has overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago.

London's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC), the Caribbean island's final court of appeal, ruled the laws were not in keeping with the "fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life."

The judgement is the result of an 11-year legal battle brought by dual-citizen Jason Jones, 62, who said he hoped it would "accelerate the fight for full equality."

Jones had successfully challenged the laws in 2018 in Trinidad's High Court, however the ruling was overturned on appeal by the Trinidadian government.

It is the first time the JCPC has ever decided on a case to decriminalise same-sex intimacy, and campaigners hope it will spark similar successful legal challenges elsewhere in the Commonwealth.

Prior to this historic decision, Trinidad and Tobago was one of some 34 Commonwealth countries continuing to criminalise homosexuality based on colonial-era British laws.

Under these laws, consensual same-sex intimacy is punishable by imprisonment, and in some cases carries the death penalty.

The Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago had argued that the law was protected from legal challenges by the "savings law clauses" - which carried over existing British laws into newly independent states.

Representatives for Jones argued that the laws violated an individual's right to privacy and argued the government's changes to the laws in 1986 - which saw stricter punishments introduced - meant the savings clause protections no longer applied.

The judicial committee unanimously found in favour of Jones.

Handing down the judgement, Lord Sales told the court the laws "cannot be regarded as reasonably justifiable in a society that has a proper respect for the rights and freedoms of an individual".

Jones, human rights campaigner and appellant in the appeal, said: "These laws never reflected who we are as a people and a nation - diverse, multiracial, and secular.

"They told LGBTQ+ people that we were criminals in our own country. That message ends today."

Lawyer Anand Ramlogan SC, representing Jones, said the judgement was a "landmark victory for gay rights, equal dignity and respect for private and family life in Trinidad and Tobago."

President Donald Trump is defending War Secretary Pete Hegseth as outgoi...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump calls out Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., amid the congressman’s push to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth.

President Donald Trump is defending War Secretary Pete Hegseth as outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., targets the Pentagon chief for impeachment.

The president issued a Truth Social post on Monday slamming the congressman as "a total loser" while asserting that the war secretary "should be praised, not impeached."

"Defeated Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, a total loser, is trying to Impeach perhaps the most popular and successful military official in the Country, Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth," Trump declared Monday on Truth Social.

HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT VOTE LOOMS AS HOUSE REPUBLICANS PRIVATELY WARN IT COULD PASS

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., speaks on impeaching U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth outside the U.S. Capitol on Nov. 9, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"With recruitment at an ALL-TIME HIGH, from an all-time low under Sleepy Joe Biden, and TWO VICTORIES, Venezuela and Iran, Pete Hegseth should be praised, not Impeached. Congress, stand up for Pete!!!" he added.

Massie did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's comment request on Tuesday.

Hegseth shared a screenshot of the president's post and thanked him.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: HOW MIDTERMS MAY CHANGE THE HOUSE IMPEACHMENT EQUATION FOR HEGSETH

President Donald Trump speaks with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth at the Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit at U.S. Army War College on July 15, 2026, in Carlisle, Pennsylvania. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

articles.title: Khor Mor drone attack raises fears over Iraq’s energy security
articles.excerpt: A drone attack on the Khor Mor gasfield in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region of northern Iraq has drawn attention to the security challenges facing the country’s energy sector, amid escalating region...
articles.body_text:
A drone attack on the Khor Mor gasfield in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region of northern Iraq has drawn attention to the security challenges facing the country’s energy sector, amid escalating regional tensions and domestic political disagreements over restricting weapons to state control.

The attack in Sulaimaniyah governorate late on Sunday sparked a fire and forced the suspension of gas supplies to several power stations, initially reducing electricity generation in areas administered by the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) by between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts, according to regional officials.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered the formation of a joint investigative committee with KRG authorities to determine who was behind the attack.

No group has claimed responsibility, but the attack comes as regional tensions are heightened due to the US-Israel war on Iran, with Baghdad facing pressure to bring weapons held by predominantly pro-Iranian Shia armed factions under state control. KRG authorities have blamed Iran-backed groups in Iraq for previous attacks on the field in recent years.

The attack also comes days after the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) announced its withdrawal from the KRG, deepening a political crisis with its rival, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).

Mohammed Amer, a political science academic and a member of the KDP, said the Khor Mor attack represents a genuine test of the Iraqi state’s sovereignty and its ability to rein in armed groups operating outside its control, and protect its territory and vital facilities.

“The [federal Iraqi] government bears responsibility for protecting Iraqi territory and airspace,” Amer told Al Jazeera. “The repeated targeting of energy sources in the Kurdistan Region also requires it to hold accountable the parties and factions behind these attacks, and to question the authorities responsible for the areas from which they are launched.”

Amer urged the Iraqi government to accelerate efforts to bring weapons under state control, warning that repeated attacks coud deter foreign investment in Iraq’s energy industry.

“These strikes target foreign investment in Iraq’s energy sector, particularly as the Khor Mor field has been targeted many times using drones and missiles,” he said. “There are factions that declare their loyalty to Iran and not to the Iraqi state, and this raises questions about the government’s ability to impose its authority and sovereignty over all Iraqi territory.”

Strategic affairs researcher Kadhim Yawer also linked the attack to regional tensions, with fears continuing that the war between the United States and Iran may escalate once again in the coming days and weeks.

“The strategic purpose of targeting the Khor Mor field at this time is primarily due to external factors linked to the escalation of the conflict between Iran and the US, as well as the desire to inflict economic damage on the Kurdistan Region and Iraq in general,” Yawer said.

He said that the dispute over disarming militias, combined with worsening divisions between the KDP and the PUK, could add to the economic pressure on the region. That comes at a time when, according to Yawer, the field’s importance could grow as the KRG seeks to expand gas production and potentially reach new markets.

Yawer argued that the withdrawal of US-led coalition forces from Iraq had created additional security challenges, particularly as some political forces – including parliamentarians – continue to not support the full disarmament of militias, allowing them more freedom to operate.

Political researcher Ghanem al-Abed pointed to the timing of the attack, which came as the political dispute between the KDP and the PUK intensified and Baghdad faced resistance from armed groups over its disarmament plans.

“The notable point about the timing of the targeting of the Khor Mor field is that it coincides with political disagreements between the KDP and the PUK, as well as the escalating disagreements between the Iraqi prime minister and some armed factions over handing their weapons to the state,” he said.

The Reuters news agency has reported that the attack originated from the Tuz Khurmatu area of Salah al-Din governorate, outside of northern Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdish region – although neither the launch location nor the perpetrators have been officially established so far. Al-Abed called on the Iraqi central government to identify those responsible and hold them accountable.

Al-Abed said the economic consequences of further attacks could extend beyond areas administered by the KRG, given the field’s role in electricity generation in the neighbouring governorates of Kirkuk and Nineveh.

“The Iraqi government must announce the identity of the parties seeking to destroy the country’s economy and hold them accountable,” he said. “The situation in Iraq could explode at any moment because some armed factions are not complying with the demand to hand over their weapons to the state. If war breaks out again between Iran and the US, these factions may intervene in the confrontation, and Iraq could then turn into a battlefield.”

articles.title: PAUL MAURO: Sanctuary states have a DMV problem — and Trump can demand answers
